DISTINCT ANGLE: his repeatable methodology IS the 'how to make a famous song every time' blueprint — 'melodic math', thesis-chorus-repetition, no more than ~3 melodic parts, the 'monkey-chant test', the chorus must arrive before 60s, every section introduced with a new sound, repetition-with-variation. SEAM: the foundational framework is well-attested in John Seabrook's book 'The Song Machine' and long Rolling Stone/NYT profiles — frame this lane as the REFERENCE formula lane; show how Max's method STILL produces 2020-2025 Hot 100 hits via The Weeknd. 3) Lyric method — minimal-and-memorable; secondary to melody; how toplines dictate rhymes.
4) Topline/singing method — recording toplines; production-driven melody writing; the 'math' of repeated hooks.

**Karl Martin Sandberg** (born 26 February 1971),[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-bio-2) known professionally as **Max Martin**, is a Swedish record producer and songwriter. He rose to prominence in the late 1990s with songwriting credits on a string of hit singles, such as [Britney Spears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_Spears "Britney Spears")'s "[...Baby One More Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...Baby_One_More_Time "...Baby One More Time")" (1998), the [Backstreet Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backstreet_Boys "Backstreet Boys")' "[I Want It That Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Want_It_That_Way "I Want It That Way")" (1999), [Celine Dion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celine_Dion "Celine Dion")'s "[That's the Way It Is](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That's_the_Way_It_Is_\(Celine_Dion_song\) "That's the Way It Is (Celine Dion song)")" (1999), and [NSYNC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSYNC "NSYNC")'s "[It's Gonna Be Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Gonna_Be_Me "It's Gonna Be Me")" (2000).

Martin has written or co-written 30 [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") number-one singles; 28 of which he has produced or co-produced, an all-time record for the chart as of June 2026. His credits include [Katy Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Perry "Katy Perry")'s "[I Kissed a Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Kissed_a_Girl "I Kissed a Girl")" (2008) and "[Roar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roar_\(song\) "Roar (song)")" (2013), [Maroon 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maroon_5 "Maroon 5")'s "[One More Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_More_Night_\(Maroon_5_song\) "One More Night (Maroon 5 song)")" (2012), [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift")'s "[Shake It Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shake_It_Off "Shake It Off")", "[Blank Space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blank_Space "Blank Space")" (2014) and "[The Fate of Ophelia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fate_of_Ophelia "The Fate of Ophelia")" (2025), [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande")'s "[Yes, And?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yes,_And%3F "Yes, And?")" and "[We Can't Be Friends (Wait for Your Love)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Can't_Be_Friends_\(Wait_for_Your_Love\) "We Can't Be Friends (Wait for Your Love)")" (2024), [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran") and [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s "[I Don't Care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don't_Care_\(Ed_Sheeran_and_Justin_Bieber_song\) "I Don't Care (Ed Sheeran and Justin Bieber song)")" (2019) and [The Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd")'s "[Blinding Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blinding_Lights "Blinding Lights")" (2019) and "[Save Your Tears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_Your_Tears "Save Your Tears")" (2020). "Blinding Lights" is the [best performing song of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") according to the chart.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) Martin has written the second-[most number-one singles on the chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Songwriter_achievements "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones"), behind only [Paul McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney") (32), having surpassed [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") (26) with his 27th number one in March 2024.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Trust-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) Many of Martin's hits were used in the 2019 jukebox musical _[& Juliet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/&_Juliet "& Juliet")_.

In early 2013, _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ tallied his singles sales at over 135 million copies.[\[8\]](#cite_note-Ostroff-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) According to _Variety_, his net worth was approximately $260 million in 2017; the previous year, his corporate entity generated revenue of $54 million with a profit of $19 million.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) Martin has won the [ASCAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_of_Composers,_Authors_and_Publishers "American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers") Songwriter of the Year award a record 11 times.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) He has also won five [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"), including [Producer of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Producer_of_the_Year,_Non-Classical "Grammy Award for Producer of the Year, Non-Classical"), and nominations for an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") and two [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards").

### Early career and It's Alive

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Max_Martin&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career and It's Alive")\]

Sandberg was born and grew up in [Stenhamra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stenhamra "Stenhamra"), [Ekerö Municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ekerö_Municipality "Ekerö Municipality"), [Stockholm County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_County "Stockholm County"). His mother was a middle school teacher and his father was a police officer.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) As a child, Martin was a student of Sweden's public music-education scheme, and once said he had "public music education to thank for everything".[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

As a teenager he sang in a variety of bands before joining a [glam-style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glam_metal "Glam metal") metal band called [It's Alive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Alive_\(band\) "It's Alive (band)") in 1985 as their singer and frontman.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) It's Alive was formed by Peter Kahm and ex-Lazy members [Per Aldeheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_Aldeheim "Per Aldeheim") and Kim Björkgren on guitars, and John Rosth who had been a member of Lineout. Martin eventually dropped out of high school to pursue a career in music with his band under the nickname "Martin White". In 1988 It's Alive participated in Rock-SM (English: Swedish Rock Championship), a nationwide [battle of the bands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_bands "Battle of the bands"), and had a residency at a nightclub in [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus "Cyprus"). The band got a breakthrough in 1991, as Dave Constable of [Megarock Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megarock_Records "Megarock Records") offered them to make a demo record. The later debut album was originally pressed in 1,000 copies and later on given away as a free cover tape in the UK by the _[Metal Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal_Forces "Metal Forces")_ magazine.

The decision to focus on a music career paid off as they landed a record deal on producer [Denniz Pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denniz_Pop "Denniz Pop")'s label [Cheiron Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheiron_Studios "Cheiron Studios"), a [BMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertelsmann_Music_Group "Bertelsmann Music Group") affiliate. After recording their second album _[Earthquake Visions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquake_Visions "Earthquake Visions")_, they released three singles in conjunction with the record and toured through Europe in 1994 supporting [Kingdom Come](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_Come_\(German_band\) "Kingdom Come (German band)"). _Earthquake Visions_ eventually sold a disappointing 30,000 copies, despite being released in as many as 30 countries. More importantly though, Martin also began collaborating on songs with [Denniz Pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denniz_Pop "Denniz Pop"). Recognizing a talent for writing pop songs in the young rocker, Denniz Pop renamed his new protégé Max Martin and eventually became Martin's mentor.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

### Working with Cheiron and Denniz PoP

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Max_Martin&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Working with Cheiron and Denniz PoP")\]

> I didn't even know what a producer did, I spent two years–day and night–in that studio trying to learn what the hell was going on.

— Martin, 2001[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

In 1993, Martin was hired by [Cheiron Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheiron_Studios "Cheiron Studios") and spent some time learning the basics, before the first production collaboration between PoP and Martin: the [Rednex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rednex "Rednex") song "[Wish You Were Here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wish_You_Were_Here_\(Rednex_song\) "Wish You Were Here (Rednex song)")" in 1994. When Martin produced the intro to [E-Type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-Type_\(musician\) "E-Type (musician)")'s song "[This Is the Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Is_the_Way_\(E-Type_song\) "This Is the Way (E-Type song)")", E-Type and PoP credited it to the made up producer alias "Max Martin", thus inventing his artist name. Martin was informed after-the-fact, when the printed records came back.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) They both worked on [Ace of Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace_of_Base "Ace of Base")'s second album, _[The Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bridge_\(Ace_of_Base_album\) "The Bridge (Ace of Base album)")_ (1995), shortly thereafter, as well as on albums by [3T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3T "3T"), [Army of Lovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_Lovers "Army of Lovers")[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) and [Leila K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leila_K "Leila K").[\[21\]](#cite_note-21) To date, _The Bridge_ has sold more than six million copies worldwide, including one million in the United States.[\[22\]](#cite_note-Ace_of_Base's_USA_Certifications-22) When Martin eventually left his band [It's Alive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Alive_\(band\) "It's Alive (band)") in late 1995, he was replaced by Anders Hansson.

In 1995, Cheiron Studios was hired by [Zomba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zomba_Label_Group "Zomba Label Group") to work on Backstreet Boys' self-titled debut album _[Backstreet Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backstreet_Boys_\(1996_album\) "Backstreet Boys (1996 album)")_ (1996). [Zomba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zomba_Label_Group "Zomba Label Group") became the main working partner since the success in 1995. Martin took part in the production of "[Quit Playing Games (with My Heart)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quit_Playing_Games_\(with_My_Heart\) "Quit Playing Games (with My Heart)")" (1996), co-written with [Herbie Crichlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbie_Crichlow "Herbie Crichlow"), a single which quickly went [platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_single "Platinum single") and climbed to No. 2 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), as well as the singles "[As Long As You Love Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/As_Long_as_You_Love_Me_\(Backstreet_Boys_song\) "As Long as You Love Me (Backstreet Boys song)")" (1997) and "[Everybody (Backstreet's Back)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody_\(Backstreet's_Back\) "Everybody (Backstreet's Back)")" (1997). The album was not released in the U.S. until 1997, but was released overseas and caught on all across Europe, eventually selling around 8 million copies worldwide. This led to the Backstreet Boys being relaunched in their home country later on, this time more successfully.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) Later that year, Martin co-wrote and co-produced [Robyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robyn "Robyn")'s hits "[Show Me Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Show_Me_Love_\(Robyn_song\) "Show Me Love (Robyn song)")" and "[Do You Know (What It Takes)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do_You_Know_\(What_It_Takes\) "Do You Know (What It Takes)")" which ended up on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 top 10.[\[8\]](#cite_note-Ostroff-8)

In 1998, [Cheiron Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheiron_Productions "Cheiron Productions") worked on albums by [Five](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_\(band\) "Five (band)") and [Jessica Folcker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Folcker "Jessica Folcker"). Jessica Folcker had first been hired as a backing singer for tracks with Ace of Base and [Dr. Alban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Alban "Dr. Alban"), and her debut album _Jessica_ became an instant hit with singles like "Tell Me What You Like" and "How Will I Know Who You Are" which both sold [platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_record "Platinum record"). After Denniz PoP died of cancer that same summer, Martin took over as director of Cheiron Studios. He soon started working with writer/producer [Rami Yacoub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rami_Yacoub "Rami Yacoub"), who continued to be his partner for many years. Martin also wrote two songs with [Bryan Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Adams "Bryan Adams") during this time, "Cloud Number Nine" and "Before The Night Is Over".

In late 1999, [Celine Dion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celine_Dion "Celine Dion") released "[That's the Way It Is](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That's_the_Way_It_Is_\(Celine_Dion_song\) "That's the Way It Is (Celine Dion song)")", a song co-written by Max Martin to promote her [greatest hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_hits "Greatest hits") album _[All the Way... A Decade of Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_the_Way..._A_Decade_of_Song "All the Way... A Decade of Song")._ The song became a hit, going to number 1 on the adult contemporary charts in the United States and Canada, and reaching top 10 all over the world. Since the song was released in November 1999, it has cycled 500,000 times on almost 1400 radio stations across Canada and the U.S. In 2003 Martin co-wrote and produced three songs for Dion's album _[One Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Heart "One Heart")._ One of them, called "[Faith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_\(Celine_Dion_song\) "Faith (Celine Dion song)")", was released in 2003 as a promotional single in Canada and reached number 4 on the Quebec Airplay Chart and number 37 on the Canadian Adult Contemporary Chart.

Martin, Andreas Carlsson, and Rami Yacoub wrote [Westlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlife "Westlife")'s song "I Need You" for the first Westlife album _[Westlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlife_\(album\) "Westlife (album)")_ (1999). Martin, Nick Jarl, Steve Mac, and Patric Jonsson wrote Westlife's song "[You Make Me Feel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Make_Me_Feel_\(Westlife_song\) "You Make Me Feel (Westlife song)")" for their second album _[Coast to Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coast_to_Coast_\(Westlife_album\) "Coast to Coast (Westlife album)")_ (2000). Max Martin, [Rami Yacoub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rami_Yacoub "Rami Yacoub"), and Andreas Carlsson also wrote one of Westlife's hits, "[When You're Looking Like That](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When_You're_Looking_Like_That "When You're Looking Like That")", for their second album _[Coast to Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coast_to_Coast_\(Westlife_album\) "Coast to Coast (Westlife album)")_ (2000).

Martin wrote, co-wrote, and co-produced 7 out of the 12 songs on the Backstreet Boys' third album _[Millennium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_\(Backstreet_Boys_album\) "Millennium (Backstreet Boys album)")_ (1999), including all the singles.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) "[I Want It That Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Want_It_That_Way "I Want It That Way")", a hit song Martin co-wrote with [Andreas Carlsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andreas_Carlsson "Andreas Carlsson") and co-produced with [Kristian Lundin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristian_Lundin "Kristian Lundin"), became the group's biggest single to date and it is still popular today, being voted No. 10 in the MTV/[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone") list of the "100 Greatest Pop Songs".[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)[\[26\]](#cite_note-mtvrollinstones100best-26) _100 Greatest Songs of the '90s_, a VH1 special, ranked the song at number 3, making it the highest ranked boy-band single and pop song.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) _Millennium_ sold over 1.1 million units in its first week in the United States, setting a record for most albums sold in its debut week (that record was later beaten by [NSYNC's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSYNC "NSYNC") 2000 album _[No Strings Attached](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Strings_Attached_\(NSYNC_album\) "No Strings Attached (NSYNC album)")_), and was the best-selling album in the world.[\[28\]](#cite_note-28)[\[29\]](#cite_note-29)

When working on her own solo album, to be released in 2001 on [Stockholm Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_Records "Stockholm Records"), [Lisa Miskovsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Miskovsky "Lisa Miskovsky") wrote the lyrics for the Backstreet Boys' hit single "[Shape of My Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shape_of_My_Heart_\(Backstreet_Boys_song\) "Shape of My Heart (Backstreet Boys song)")" with Max Martin and Rami. The song, originally written for Miskovsky's own album, was passed on to the Backstreet Boys by Max Martin when Miskovsky decided that it did not fit her style. The song became the first single off the group's fourth album _[Black & Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_&_Blue_\(Backstreet_Boys_album\) "Black & Blue (Backstreet Boys album)")_ (2000).[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) In the first week of release, "[Shape of My Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shape_of_My_Heart_\(Backstreet_Boys_song\) "Shape of My Heart (Backstreet Boys song)")" immediately jumped into the Top Five in Sweden, Norway, Canada, Germany and another 15 countries.[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) _Black & Blue_, containing several songs produced and written by Martin, sold 1.6 million units in its first week in America. Martin again received [ASCAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCAP "ASCAP")'s award "Songwriter of the Year" both in 2000 and 2001.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) In April 2013 the Backstreet Boys member [Brian Littrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Littrell "Brian Littrell") invited Martin to collaborate on their single "[In A World Like This](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_A_World_Like_This "In A World Like This")". The single peaked at _No.6_ in the _[Oricon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oricon_Singles_Chart "Oricon Singles Chart")_ chart and performed well in the rest of the world. Martin collaborated on the _Never Gone_ songs "Climbing the Walls", "[Just Want You to Know](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_Want_You_to_Know "Just Want You to Know")", "Siberia" and "[I Still...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Still... "I Still...")". Martin wanted the album to be more of a contemporary, alternative pop album with a little R&B. The resulting album had a more organic music style with more live instruments, and was a departure from the Backstreet Boys' earlier work.

> \[Martin\] gets exactly what I am saying when I tell him what I want and don't want musically. His melodies are incredible and he is always coming up with weird sounds, which I love... There is nobody I feel more comfortable collaborating with in the studio

— Spears on working with Martin[\[33\]](#cite_note-33)

In 1998, Martin wrote and co-produced [Spears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_Spears "Britney Spears")' debut single, "[...Baby One More Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...Baby_One_More_Time "...Baby One More Time")", for her debut album of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...Baby_One_More_Time_\(album\) "...Baby One More Time (album)"). The single was originally offered to the [Backstreet Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backstreet_Boys "Backstreet Boys") and [TLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TLC_\(music\) "TLC (music)"), though both passed on the song.[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) That same year, Martin also co-wrote and co-produced the third single "[(You Drive Me) Crazy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/\(You_Drive_Me\)_Crazy "(You Drive Me) Crazy")". By 1999, the album _...Baby One More Time_ had sold over 15 million copies in the U.S., certifying [Diamond Status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_sales_certification "Music recording sales certification").[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) Also, within a year of its release, _...Baby One More Time_ had become the best-selling [LP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compact_disc "Compact disc") by a teenager in history, selling over 30 million copies.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36)

Martin was the first non-American citizen ever to win ASCAP's award "Songwriter of the Year" in 1999, an award he also won in 2000 and 2001.[\[37\]](#cite_note-37)

Martin worked on Spears's follow-up records _[Oops!... I Did It Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oops!..._I_Did_It_Again_\(album\) "Oops!... I Did It Again (album)")_ (2000) and _[Britney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_\(album\) "Britney (album)")_ (2001). He co-wrote and co-produced the singles "[Oops!... I Did It Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oops!..._I_Did_It_Again_\(song\) "Oops!... I Did It Again (song)")" (2000), "[Lucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucky_\(Britney_Spears_song\) "Lucky (Britney Spears song)")" (2000), "[Stronger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stronger_\(Britney_Spears_song\) "Stronger (Britney Spears song)")" (2000), "[Overprotected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overprotected "Overprotected")" (2001), and "[I'm Not a Girl, Not Yet a Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Not_a_Girl,_Not_Yet_a_Woman "I'm Not a Girl, Not Yet a Woman")" (2002).

The duo ended up parting ways when Spears distanced herself from [teen pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_pop "Teen pop"). Spears recorded _[In the Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_the_Zone "In the Zone")_ (2003) and _[Blackout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackout_\(Britney_Spears_album\) "Blackout (Britney Spears album)")_ (2007).

At the request of Spears, Martin produced and wrote for Spears' sixth studio album _[Circus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circus_\(Britney_Spears_album\) "Circus (Britney Spears album)")_ (2008). Martin co-wrote and produced the provocatively titled electro pop song, "[If U Seek Amy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_U_Seek_Amy "If U Seek Amy")", which was chosen by fans to be the third single of the album. Martin then produced the number one hit, "[3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3_\(Britney_Spears_song\) "3 (Britney Spears song)")", for Spears' compilation album _[The Singles Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Singles_Collection_\(Britney_Spears_album\) "The Singles Collection (Britney Spears album)")_ (2009).

Martin was one of the executive producers of Spears's seventh album, _[Femme Fatale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femme_Fatale_\(Britney_Spears_album\) "Femme Fatale (Britney Spears album)")_ (2011), alongside [Dr. Luke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Luke "Dr. Luke"). He produced several songs for the album, including the successful singles "[Hold It Against Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hold_It_Against_Me "Hold It Against Me")", "[Till the World Ends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Till_the_World_Ends "Till the World Ends")", "[I Wanna Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Wanna_Go "I Wanna Go")", and "[Criminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal_\(Britney_Spears_song\) "Criminal (Britney Spears song)")".[\[38\]](#cite_note-confirm-38)[\[39\]](#cite_note-39)

### Startup of Maratone

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Max_Martin&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Startup of Maratone")\]

Following the death of [Denniz PoP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denniz_PoP "Denniz PoP"), [Cheiron Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheiron_Studios "Cheiron Studios") was closed down in 2000. Martin and Tom Talomaa then started a new production company named [Maratone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratone "Maratone") in January 2001 and moved into the famous [Cosmos Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmos_Studios "Cosmos Studios") building. The first songs to be written and produced at Maratone were four tracks for [Britney Spears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_Spears "Britney Spears")'s album _[Britney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_\(album\) "Britney (album)")_ (2001). The Maratone production crew initially consisted of producers/songwriters Max Martin, Rami, Alexandra, [Arnthor Birgisson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnthor_Birgisson "Arnthor Birgisson") and [Shellback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shellback_\(record_producer\) "Shellback (record producer)"). Following the work with [Celine Dion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celine_Dion "Celine Dion") on the album _[One Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Heart "One Heart")_ in 2003, few new hits appeared from Maratone until 2005.

In 2004, [Kelly Clarkson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Clarkson "Kelly Clarkson") traveled to Sweden to collaborate with Martin and [Dr. Luke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Gottwald "Luke Gottwald") on her second studio album, _[Breakaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakaway_\(Kelly_Clarkson_album\) "Breakaway (Kelly Clarkson album)")_. These collaborations resulted in the rock-influenced singles "[Since U Been Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Since_U_Been_Gone "Since U Been Gone")" (2004) and "[Behind These Hazel Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behind_These_Hazel_Eyes "Behind These Hazel Eyes")" (2005). In 2009, Martin co-wrote Clarkson's single "[My Life Would Suck Without You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Life_Would_Suck_Without_You "My Life Would Suck Without You")", which was a number one hit.

In 2005, Martin collaborated with the Norwegian singer [Marion Raven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_Raven "Marion Raven") for the release of her debut album, titled _[Here I Am](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here_I_Am_\(Marion_Raven_album\) "Here I Am (Marion Raven album)"),_ writing and co-writing the songs "[Break You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Break_You "Break You")", "[End of Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_of_Me_\(Marion_Raven_song\) "End of Me (Marion Raven song)")", "Here I Am", "Little By Little", "In Spite of Me", and "Six Feet Under".

Martin co-wrote and produced three songs on [Pink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pink_\(singer\) "Pink (singer)")'s platinum-selling album _[I'm Not Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Not_Dead "I'm Not Dead")_, including the singles, "[U + Ur Hand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U_+_Ur_Hand "U + Ur Hand")" (2006), "[Who Knew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who_Knew "Who Knew")" (2006), and "[Cuz I Can](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/'Cuz_I_Can_\(Pink_song\) "'Cuz I Can (Pink song)")" (2007).

Martin also collaborated with Pink for her next album, _[Funhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funhouse_\(Pink_album\) "Funhouse (Pink album)")_ (2008). Martin co-wrote the first smash hit single, "[So What](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_What_\(Pink_song\) "So What (Pink song)")" (2008), plus the singles "[Please Don't Leave Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Please_Don't_Leave_Me "Please Don't Leave Me")" (2009) and "[I Don't Believe You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don't_Believe_You "I Don't Believe You")" (2009). The duo wrote "[Whataya Want From Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whataya_Want_From_Me "Whataya Want From Me")" during the sessions for _Funhouse_, but ultimately the song was recorded and released as a single by [Adam Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Lambert "Adam Lambert").

Later, Martin co-wrote hits for Pink including "[Raise Your Glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raise_Your_Glass "Raise Your Glass")" (2010), "[Fuckin' Perfect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuckin'_Perfect "Fuckin' Perfect")" (2011), and "[Just like Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_like_Fire

**Karl Martin Sandberg** (born 26 February 1971),[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-bio-2) known professionally as **Max Martin**, is a Swedish record producer and songwriter. He rose to prominence in the late 1990s with songwriting credits on a string of hit singles, such as [Britney Spears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_Spears "Britney Spears")'s "[...Baby One More Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...Baby_One_More_Time "...Baby One More Time")" (1998), the [Backstreet Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backstreet_Boys "Backstreet Boys")' "[I Want It That Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Want_It_That_Way "I Want It That Way")" (1999), [Celine Dion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celine_Dion "Celine Dion")'s "[That's the Way It Is](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That's_the_Way_It_Is_\(Celine_Dion_song\) "That's the Way It Is (Celine Dion song)")" (1999), and [NSYNC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSYNC "NSYNC")'s "[It's Gonna Be Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Gonna_Be_Me "It's Gonna Be Me")" (2000).

Martin has written or co-written 30 [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") number-one singles; 28 of which he has produced or co-produced, an all-time record for the chart as of June 2026. His credits include [Katy Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Perry "Katy Perry")'s "[I Kissed a Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Kissed_a_Girl "I Kissed a Girl")" (2008) and "[Roar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roar_\(song\) "Roar (song)")" (2013), [Maroon 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maroon_5 "Maroon 5")'s "[One More Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_More_Night_\(Maroon_5_song\) "One More Night (Maroon 5 song)")" (2012), [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift")'s "[Shake It Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shake_It_Off "Shake It Off")", "[Blank Space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blank_Space "Blank Space")" (2014) and "[The Fate of Ophelia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fate_of_Ophelia "The Fate of Ophelia")" (2025), [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande")'s "[Yes, And?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yes,_And%3F "Yes, And?")" and "[We Can't Be Friends (Wait for Your Love)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Can't_Be_Friends_\(Wait_for_Your_Love\) "We Can't Be Friends (Wait for Your Love)")" (2024), [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran") and [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s "[I Don't Care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don't_Care_\(Ed_Sheeran_and_Justin_Bieber_song\) "I Don't Care (Ed Sheeran and Justin Bieber song)")" (2019) and [The Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd")'s "[Blinding Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blinding_Lights "Blinding Lights")" (2019) and "[Save Your Tears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_Your_Tears "Save Your Tears")" (2020). "Blinding Lights" is the [best performing song of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") according to the chart.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) Martin has written the second-[most number-one singles on the chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Songwriter_achievements "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones"), behind only [Paul McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney") (32), having surpassed [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") (26) with his 27th number one in March 2024.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Trust-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) Many of Martin's hits were used in the 2019 jukebox musical _[& Juliet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/&_Juliet "& Juliet")_.

In early 2013, _[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ tallied his singles sales at over 135 million copies.[\[8\]](#cite_note-Ostroff-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) According to _Variety_, his net worth was approximately $260 million in 2017; the previous year, his corporate entity generated revenue of $54 million with a profit of $19 million.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) Martin has won the [ASCAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Society_of_Composers,_Authors_and_Publishers "American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers") Songwriter of the Year award a record 11 times.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) He has also won five [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"), including [Producer of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Producer_of_the_Year,_Non-Classical "Grammy Award for Producer of the Year, Non-Classical"), and nominations for an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") and two [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards").

### Early career and It's Alive

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Max_Martin&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career and It's Alive")\]

Sandberg was born and grew up in [Stenhamra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stenhamra "Stenhamra"), [Ekerö Municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ekerö_Municipality "Ekerö Municipality"), [Stockholm County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_County "Stockholm County"). His mother was a middle school teacher and his father was a police officer.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) As a child, Martin was a student of Sweden's public music-education scheme, and once said he had "public music education to thank for everything".[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

As a teenager he sang in a variety of bands before joining a [glam-style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glam_metal "Glam metal") metal band called [It's Alive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Alive_\(band\) "It's Alive (band)") in 1985 as their singer and frontman.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) It's Alive was formed by Peter Kahm and ex-Lazy members [Per Aldeheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_Aldeheim "Per Aldeheim") and Kim Björkgren on guitars, and John Rosth who had been a member of Lineout. Martin eventually dropped out of high school to pursue a career in music with his band under the nickname "Martin White". In 1988 It's Alive participated in Rock-SM (English: Swedish Rock Championship), a nationwide [battle of the bands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_bands "Battle of the bands"), and had a residency at a nightclub in [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus "Cyprus"). The band got a breakthrough in 1991, as Dave Constable of [Megarock Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megarock_Records "Megarock Records") offered them to make a demo record. The later debut album was originally pressed in 1,000 copies and later on given away as a free cover tape in the UK by the _[Metal Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal_Forces "Metal Forces")_ magazine.

The decision to focus on a music career paid off as they landed a record deal on producer [Denniz Pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denniz_Pop "Denniz Pop")'s label [Cheiron Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheiron_Studios "Cheiron Studios"), a [BMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertelsmann_Music_Group "Bertelsmann Music Group") affiliate. After recording their second album _[Earthquake Visions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquake_Visions "Earthquake Visions")_, they released three singles in conjunction with the record and toured through Europe in 1994 supporting [Kingdom Come](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_Come_\(German_band\) "Kingdom Come (German band)"). _Earthquake Visions_ eventually sold a disappointing 30,000 copies, despite being released in as many as 30 countries. More importantly though, Martin also began collaborating on songs with [Denniz Pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denniz_Pop "Denniz Pop"). Recognizing a talent for writing pop songs in the young rocker, Denniz Pop renamed his new protégé Max Martin and eventually became Martin's mentor.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

### Working with Cheiron and Denniz PoP

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Max_Martin&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Working with Cheiron and Denniz PoP")\]

> I didn't even know what a producer did, I spent two years–day and night–in that studio trying to learn what the hell was going on.

— Martin, 2001[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

In 1993, Martin was hired by [Cheiron Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheiron_Studios "Cheiron Studios") and spent some time learning the basics, before the first production collaboration between PoP and Martin: the [Rednex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rednex "Rednex") song "[Wish You Were Here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wish_You_Were_Here_\(Rednex_song\) "Wish You Were Here (Rednex song)")" in 1994. When Martin produced the intro to [E-Type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-Type_\(musician\) "E-Type (musician)")'s song "[This Is the Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Is_the_Way_\(E-Type_song\) "This Is the Way (E-Type song)")", E-Type and PoP credited it to the made up producer alias "Max Martin", thus inventing his artist name. Martin was informed after-the-fact, when the printed records came back.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) They both worked on [Ace of Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace_of_Base "Ace of Base")'s second album, _[The Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bridge_\(Ace_of_Base_album\) "The Bridge (Ace of Base album)")_ (1995), shortly thereafter, as well as on albums by [3T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3T "3T"), [Army of Lovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_Lovers "Army of Lovers")[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) and [Leila K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leila_K "Leila K").[\[21\]](#cite_note-21) To date, _The Bridge_ has sold more than six million copies worldwide, including one million in the United States.[\[22\]](#cite_note-Ace_of_Base's_USA_Certifications-22) When Martin eventually left his band [It's Alive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Alive_\(band\) "It's Alive (band)") in late 1995, he was replaced by Anders Hansson.

In 1995, Cheiron Studios was hired by [Zomba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zomba_Label_Group "Zomba Label Group") to work on Backstreet Boys' self-titled debut album _[Backstreet Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backstreet_Boys_\(1996_album\) "Backstreet Boys (1996 album)")_ (1996). [Zomba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zomba_Label_Group "Zomba Label Group") became the main working partner since the success in 1995. Martin took part in the production of "[Quit Playing Games (with My Heart)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quit_Playing_Games_\(with_My_Heart\) "Quit Playing Games (with My Heart)")" (1996), co-written with [Herbie Crichlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbie_Crichlow "Herbie Crichlow"), a single which quickly went [platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_single "Platinum single") and climbed to No. 2 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), as well as the singles "[As Long As You Love Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/As_Long_as_You_Love_Me_\(Backstreet_Boys_song\) "As Long as You Love Me (Backstreet Boys song)")" (1997) and "[Everybody (Backstreet's Back)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody_\(Backstreet's_Back\) "Everybody (Backstreet's Back)")" (1997). The album was not released in the U.S. until 1997, but was released overseas and caught on all across Europe, eventually selling around 8 million copies worldwide. This led to the Backstreet Boys being relaunched in their home country later on, this time more successfully.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) Later that year, Martin co-wrote and co-produced [Robyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robyn "Robyn")'s hits "[Show Me Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Show_Me_Love_\(Robyn_song\) "Show Me Love (Robyn song)")" and "[Do You Know (What It Takes)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do_You_Know_\(What_It_Takes\) "Do You Know (What It Takes)")" which ended up on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 top 10.[\[8\]](#cite_note-Ostroff-8)

In 1998, [Cheiron Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheiron_Productions "Cheiron Productions") worked on albums by [Five](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_\(band\) "Five (band)") and [Jessica Folcker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Folcker "Jessica Folcker"). Jessica Folcker had first been hired as a backing singer for tracks with Ace of Base and [Dr. Alban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Alban "Dr. Alban"), and her debut album _Jessica_ became an instant hit with singles like "Tell Me What You Like" and "How Will I Know Who You Are" which both sold [platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_record "Platinum record"). After Denniz PoP died of cancer that same summer, Martin took over as director of Cheiron Studios. He soon started working with writer/producer [Rami Yacoub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rami_Yacoub "Rami Yacoub"), who continued to be his partner for many years. Martin also wrote two songs with [Bryan Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Adams "Bryan Adams") during this time, "Cloud Number Nine" and "Before The Night Is Over".

In late 1999, [Celine Dion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celine_Dion "Celine Dion") released "[That's the Way It Is](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That's_the_Way_It_Is_\(Celine_Dion_song\) "That's the Way It Is (Celine Dion song)")", a song co-written by Max Martin to promote her [greatest hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_hits "Greatest hits") album _[All the Way... A Decade of Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_the_Way..._A_Decade_of_Song "All the Way... A Decade of Song")._ The song became a hit, going to number 1 on the adult contemporary charts in the United States and Canada, and reaching top 10 all over the world. Since the song was released in November 1999, it has cycled 500,000 times on almost 1400 radio stations across Canada and the U.S. In 2003 Martin co-wrote and produced three songs for Dion's album _[One Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Heart "One Heart")._ One of them, called "[Faith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_\(Celine_Dion_song\) "Faith (Celine Dion song)")", was released in 2003 as a promotional single in Canada and reached number 4 on the Quebec Airplay Chart and number 37 on the Canadian Adult Contemporary Chart.

Martin, Andreas Carlsson, and Rami Yacoub wrote [Westlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlife "Westlife")'s song "I Need You" for the first Westlife album _[Westlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlife_\(album\) "Westlife (album)")_ (1999). Martin, Nick Jarl, Steve Mac, and Patric Jonsson wrote Westlife's song "[You Make Me Feel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Make_Me_Feel_\(Westlife_song\) "You Make Me Feel (Westlife song)")" for their second album _[Coast to Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coast_to_Coast_\(Westlife_album\) "Coast to Coast (Westlife album)")_ (2000). Max Martin, [Rami Yacoub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rami_Yacoub "Rami Yacoub"), and Andreas Carlsson also wrote one of Westlife's hits, "[When You're Looking Like That](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When_You're_Looking_Like_That "When You're Looking Like That")", for their second album _[Coast to Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coast_to_Coast_\(Westlife_album\) "Coast to Coast (Westlife album)")_ (2000).

Martin wrote, co-wrote, and co-produced 7 out of the 12 songs on the Backstreet Boys' third album _[Millennium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_\(Backstreet_Boys_album\) "Millennium (Backstreet Boys album)")_ (1999), including all the singles.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) "[I Want It That Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Want_It_That_Way "I Want It That Way")", a hit song Martin co-wrote with [Andreas Carlsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andreas_Carlsson "Andreas Carlsson") and co-produced with [Kristian Lundin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristian_Lundin "Kristian Lundin"), became the group's biggest single to date and it is still popular today, being voted No. 10 in the MTV/[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone") list of the "100 Greatest Pop Songs".[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)[\[26\]](#cite_note-mtvrollinstones100best-26) _100 Greatest Songs of the '90s_, a VH1 special, ranked the song at number 3, making it the highest ranked boy-band single and pop song.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) _Millennium_ sold over 1.1 million units in its first week in the United States, setting a record for most albums sold in its debut week (that record was later beaten by [NSYNC's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSYNC "NSYNC") 2000 album _[No Strings Attached](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Strings_Attached_\(NSYNC_album\) "No Strings Attached (NSYNC album)")_), and was the best-selling album in the world.[\[28\]](#cite_note-28)[\[29\]](#cite_note-29)

When working on her own solo album, to be released in 2001 on [Stockholm Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_Records "Stockholm Records"), [Lisa Miskovsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Miskovsky "Lisa Miskovsky") wrote the lyrics for the Backstreet Boys' hit single "[Shape of My Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shape_of_My_Heart_\(Backstreet_Boys_song\) "Shape of My Heart (Backstreet Boys song)")" with Max Martin and Rami. The song, originally written for Miskovsky's own album, was passed on to the Backstreet Boys by Max Martin when Miskovsky decided that it did not fit her style. The song became the first single off the group's fourth album _[Black & Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_&_Blue_\(Backstreet_Boys_album\) "Black & Blue (Backstreet Boys album)")_ (2000).[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) In the first week of release, "[Shape of My Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shape_of_My_Heart_\(Backstreet_Boys_song\) "Shape of My Heart (Backstreet Boys song)")" immediately jumped into the Top Five in Sweden, Norway, Canada, Germany and another 15 countries.[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) _Black & Blue_, containing several songs produced and written by Martin, sold 1.6 million units in its first week in America. Martin again received [ASCAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCAP "ASCAP")'s award "Songwriter of the Year" both in 2000 and 2001.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) In April 2013 the Backstreet Boys member [Brian Littrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Littrell "Brian Littrell") invited Martin to collaborate on their single "[In A World Like This](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_A_World_Like_This "In A World Like This")". The single peaked at _No.6_ in the _[Oricon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oricon_Singles_Chart "Oricon Singles Chart")_ chart and performed well in the rest of the world. Martin collaborated on the _Never Gone_ songs "Climbing the Walls", "[Just Want You to Know](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_Want_You_to_Know "Just Want You to Know")", "Siberia" and "[I Still...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Still... "I Still...")". Martin wanted the album to be more of a contemporary, alternative pop album with a little R&B. The resulting album had a more organic music style with more live instruments, and was a departure from the Backstreet Boys' earlier work.

> \[Martin\] gets exactly what I am saying when I tell him what I want and don't want musically. His melodies are incredible and he is always coming up with weird sounds, which I love... There is nobody I feel more comfortable collaborating with in the studio

— Spears on working with Martin[\[33\]](#cite_note-33)

In 1998, Martin wrote and co-produced [Spears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_Spears "Britney Spears")' debut single, "[...Baby One More Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...Baby_One_More_Time "...Baby One More Time")", for her debut album of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...Baby_One_More_Time_\(album\) "...Baby One More Time (album)"). The single was originally offered to the [Backstreet Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backstreet_Boys "Backstreet Boys") and [TLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TLC_\(music\) "TLC (music)"), though both passed on the song.[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) That same year, Martin also co-wrote and co-produced the third single "[(You Drive Me) Crazy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/\(You_Drive_Me\)_Crazy "(You Drive Me) Crazy")". By 1999, the album _...Baby One More Time_ had sold over 15 million copies in the U.S., certifying [Diamond Status](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_sales_certification "Music recording sales certification").[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) Also, within a year of its release, _...Baby One More Time_ had become the best-selling [LP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compact_disc "Compact disc") by a teenager in history, selling over 30 million copies.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36)

Martin was the first non-American citizen ever to win ASCAP's award "Songwriter of the Year" in 1999, an award he also won in 2000 and 2001.[\[37\]](#cite_note-37)

Martin worked on Spears's follow-up records _[Oops!... I Did It Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oops!..._I_Did_It_Again_\(album\) "Oops!... I Did It Again (album)")_ (2000) and _[Britney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_\(album\) "Britney (album)")_ (2001). He co-wrote and co-produced the singles "[Oops!... I Did It Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oops!..._I_Did_It_Again_\(song\) "Oops!... I Did It Again (song)")" (2000), "[Lucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucky_\(Britney_Spears_song\) "Lucky (Britney Spears song)")" (2000), "[Stronger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stronger_\(Britney_Spears_song\) "Stronger (Britney Spears song)")" (2000), "[Overprotected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overprotected "Overprotected")" (2001), and "[I'm Not a Girl, Not Yet a Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Not_a_Girl,_Not_Yet_a_Woman "I'm Not a Girl, Not Yet a Woman")" (2002).

The duo ended up parting ways when Spears distanced herself from [teen pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_pop "Teen pop"). Spears recorded _[In the Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_the_Zone "In the Zone")_ (2003) and _[Blackout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackout_\(Britney_Spears_album\) "Blackout (Britney Spears album)")_ (2007).

At the request of Spears, Martin produced and wrote for Spears' sixth studio album _[Circus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circus_\(Britney_Spears_album\) "Circus (Britney Spears album)")_ (2008). Martin co-wrote and produced the provocatively titled electro pop song, "[If U Seek Amy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_U_Seek_Amy "If U Seek Amy")", which was chosen by fans to be the third single of the album. Martin then produced the number one hit, "[3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3_\(Britney_Spears_song\) "3 (Britney Spears song)")", for Spears' compilation album _[The Singles Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Singles_Collection_\(Britney_Spears_album\) "The Singles Collection (Britney Spears album)")_ (2009).

Martin was one of the executive producers of Spears's seventh album, _[Femme Fatale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femme_Fatale_\(Britney_Spears_album\) "Femme Fatale (Britney Spears album)")_ (2011), alongside [Dr. Luke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Luke "Dr. Luke"). He produced several songs for the album, including the successful singles "[Hold It Against Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hold_It_Against_Me "Hold It Against Me")", "[Till the World Ends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Till_the_World_Ends "Till the World Ends")", "[I Wanna Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Wanna_Go "I Wanna Go")", and "[Criminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal_\(Britney_Spears_song\) "Criminal (Britney Spears song)")".[\[38\]](#cite_note-confirm-38)[\[39\]](#cite_note-39)

### Startup of Maratone

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Max_Martin&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Startup of Maratone")\]

Following the death of [Denniz PoP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denniz_PoP "Denniz PoP"), [Cheiron Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheiron_Studios "Cheiron Studios") was closed down in 2000. Martin and Tom Talomaa then started a new production company named [Maratone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratone "Maratone") in January 2001 and moved into the famous [Cosmos Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmos_Studios "Cosmos Studios") building. The first songs to be written and produced at Maratone were four tracks for [Britney Spears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_Spears "Britney Spears")'s album _[Britney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_\(album\) "Britney (album)")_ (2001). The Maratone production crew initially consisted of producers/songwriters Max Martin, Rami, Alexandra, [Arnthor Birgisson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnthor_Birgisson "Arnthor Birgisson") and [Shellback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shellback_\(record_producer\) "Shellback (record producer)"). Following the work with [Celine Dion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celine_Dion "Celine Dion") on the album _[One Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Heart "One Heart")_ in 2003, few new hits appeared from Maratone until 2005.

In 2004, [Kelly Clarkson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Clarkson "Kelly Clarkson") traveled to Sweden to collaborate with Martin and [Dr. Luke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Gottwald "Luke Gottwald") on her second studio album, _[Breakaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakaway_\(Kelly_Clarkson_album\) "Breakaway (Kelly Clarkson album)")_. These collaborations resulted in the rock-influenced singles "[Since U Been Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Since_U_Been_Gone "Since U Been Gone")" (2004) and "[Behind These Hazel Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behind_These_Hazel_Eyes "Behind These Hazel Eyes")" (2005). In 2009, Martin co-wrote Clarkson's single "[My Life Would Suck Without You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Life_Would_Suck_Without_You "My Life Would Suck Without You")", which was a number one hit.

In 2005, Martin collaborated with the Norwegian singer [Marion Raven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_Raven "Marion Raven") for the release of her debut album, titled _[Here I Am](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here_I_Am_\(Marion_Raven_album\) "Here I Am (Marion Raven album)"),_ writing and co-writing the songs "[Break You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Break_You "Break You")", "[End of Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_of_Me_\(Marion_Raven_song\) "End of Me (Marion Raven song)")", "Here I Am", "Little By Little", "In Spite of Me", and "Six Feet Under".

Martin co-wrote and produced three songs on [Pink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pink_\(singer\) "Pink (singer)")'s platinum-selling album _[I'm Not Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Not_Dead "I'm Not Dead")_, including the singles, "[U + Ur Hand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U_+_Ur_Hand "U + Ur Hand")" (2006), "[Who Knew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who_Knew "Who Knew")" (2006), and "[Cuz I Can](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/'Cuz_I_Can_\(Pink_song\) "'Cuz I Can (Pink song)")" (2007).

Martin also collaborated with Pink for her next album, _[Funhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funhouse_\(Pink_album\) "Funhouse (Pink album)")_ (2008). Martin co-wrote the first smash hit single, "[So What](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_What_\(Pink_song\) "So What (Pink song)")" (2008), plus the singles "[Please Don't Leave Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Please_Don't_Leave_Me "Please Don't Leave Me")" (2009) and "[I Don't Believe You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don't_Believe_You "I Don't Believe You")" (2009). The duo wrote "[Whataya Want From Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whataya_Want_From_Me "Whataya Want From Me")" during the sessions for _Funhouse_, but ultimately the song was recorded and released as a single by [Adam Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Lambert "Adam Lambert").

Later, Martin co-wrote hits for Pink including "[Raise Your Glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raise_Your_Glass "Raise Your Glass")" (2010), "[Fuckin' Perfect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuckin'_Perfect "Fuckin' Perfect")" (2011), and "[Just like Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_like_Fire

"**Blinding Lights**" is a song by Canadian singer-songwriter [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd"), from his fourth studio album, _[After Hours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_Hours_\(The_Weeknd_album\) "After Hours (The Weeknd album)")_ (2020). The song was released through [XO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XO_\(record_label\) "XO (record label)") and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") on November 29, 2019, as the album's second single. It is a [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop"), [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop"), [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop"), [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music"), and [synthwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthwave "Synthwave") track, which lyrically addresses the importance of a partner, and the desire to see them at night. It was written by the Weeknd, [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin"), [Oscar Holter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Holter "Oscar Holter"), [Belly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belly_\(rapper\) "Belly (rapper)"), and [DaHeala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DaHeala "DaHeala"), while being produced by the former three.

"Blinding Lights" received universal acclaim by music journalists upon release, with many noting its aesthetic, as well as its callback to the [music of the 1980s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_the_1980s "Music of the 1980s"). The song was a commercial success, topping the record charts in over 40 countries, including his native Canada, making it his most successful single to date. In the United States, "Blinding Lights" topped the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") for four non-consecutive weeks, earning his fifth number one in the country. It became the song with the [most weeks spent in the top five and top ten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") and the first song to hold a spot in the top ten for an entire year.

It was the [longest-charting song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_total_weeks_on_the_Hot_100 "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") in history for a short period of time, remaining on it for a total of 90 weeks, and was named as the chart's [best-performing song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#All-time_achievements "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") of all time on November 23, 2021. It was certified diamond by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) and seven times platinum by the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") (BPI). According to the [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry"), it was the [best-selling global single of 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles#Best-selling_singles_by_year_worldwide "List of best-selling singles") and the best-selling song overall since 2020 by stream equivalent units. On [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), it is the [most streamed song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records#Most-streamed_songs "List of Spotify streaming records") of all time, and the first song to surpass four and five billion streams.

Anton Tammi directed the song's music video, which was filmed over a four-day period shot in the night. Inspired by films such as _[Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear_and_Loathing_in_Las_Vegas_\(film\) "Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas (film)")_ (1998), _[Joker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joker_\(2019_film\) "Joker (2019 film)")_ (2019), and _[Casino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casino_\(1995_film\) "Casino (1995 film)")_ (1995), it depicts the Weeknd speeding through a city, after getting beaten by bouncers and being forced on the run. "Blinding Lights" was performed on television shows such as _[The Late Show with Stephen Colbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Late_Show_with_Stephen_Colbert "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert")_, _[Jimmy Kimmel Live!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Kimmel_Live! "Jimmy Kimmel Live!")_, _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")_, his headlining set at the [Super Bowl LV halftime show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LV_halftime_show "Super Bowl LV halftime show"), and was included on the set list for his [After Hours til Dawn Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_Hours_til_Dawn_Tour "After Hours til Dawn Tour"). It received several awards and nominations, winning Song of the Year at the [2021 iHeartRadio Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_iHeartRadio_Music_Awards "2021 iHeartRadio Music Awards") and [Juno Awards of 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Awards_of_2021 "Juno Awards of 2021").

## Background and development

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and development")\]

In November 2018, [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") announced at a concert that he was working on his fourth studio album, tentatively referred to as "Chapter VI".[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

After a five-month social media hiatus, the singer-songwriter returned to [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") on November 20, 2019, and posted six days later on November 26, 2019.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) He previously announced a project referred to as _Chapter VI_ in June 2019.[\[9\]](#cite_note-nme-9) On November 24, 2019, a [Mercedes-Benz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz "Mercedes-Benz") commercial first aired on German TV featuring a clip of "Blinding Lights".[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) It shows the Weeknd driving a [Mercedes-Benz EQC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_EQC "Mercedes-Benz EQC") SUV and asking the system to play his new song.[\[12\]](#cite_note-rap-up-12) The full-length version of the commercial premiered on November 29, alongside the single.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) In the days after, he took to social media to announce his return to music with the captions "the fall starts tomorrow night" and "Tonight we start a new brain melting psychotic chapter! Let's go!"[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

During an interview conducted by Jem Aswad from _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")_ magazine, the Weeknd discussed his experience working with Swedish songwriter-producer [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin"), saying: "Max and I have become literally the best of friends, but I don't do that with many people. It's not that I can't, but a collaboration is a relationship, it's like a marriage, you've gotta build up to it."[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) In a _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ interview, the Weeknd expressed his appreciation for [music of the 1980s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980s_in_music "1980s in music"): "I've always had an admiration for the era before I was born. You can hear it as far back as my [first mixtape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Balloons "House of Balloons") that the '80s — [Siouxsie and the Banshees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouxsie_and_the_Banshees "Siouxsie and the Banshees"), [Cocteau Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocteau_Twins "Cocteau Twins") — play such a huge role in my sound. Sometimes it helps me create a new sound and sometimes it's just obvious. I'm just glad the world's into it now."[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) In an interview with _[Vanity Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity_Fair_\(magazine\) "Vanity Fair (magazine)")_, the Weeknd said that he initially thought that the song would be a commercial failure.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

## Lyrics and composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Lyrics and composition")\]

Throughout the song, the Weeknd sings about the rekindling of a relationship and the importance of his partner. He also mentions the city of [Las Vegas, Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas,_Nevada "Las Vegas, Nevada"), when he refers to it by its nickname "Sin City" in the [pre-chorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-chorus "Pre-chorus").[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) In a profile in [_Esquire_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esquire_\(magazine\) "Esquire (magazine)"), The Weeknd explained that "'Blinding Lights' \[is about\] how you want to see someone at night, and you're intoxicated, and you're driving to this person and you're just blinded by streetlights, but nothing could stop you from trying to go see that person, because you're so lonely. I don't want to ever promote drunk driving, but that's what the dark undertone is."[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

From its scale-laddering verses to its tension-filled chorus, the song exhibits the polish and "melodic math" for which [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin") is renowned, according to Chris Molanphy from _[Slate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slate_\(magazine\) "Slate (magazine)")_.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) The [Dorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorian_mode "Dorian mode") structure provides a dreamy and euphoric nature to the song while still ultimately resolving to a minor chord. Exclusively in the music video, the song temporarily modulates to E♭ Dorian as the [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute") drops for 3 and a half measures.

_[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ staff writer Frank DiGiacomo assessed its qualities, "The opening drumbeat is a [DeLorean \[time machine\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeLorean_time_machine "DeLorean time machine") [back to](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_to_the_Future "Back to the Future") [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson")'s '[Beat It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beat_It "Beat It")'. The [amphetamine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphetamine "Amphetamine") [synth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer "Synthesizer") conjures fond memories of leopard-print-era [Rod Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_Stewart "Rod Stewart")'s '[Young Turks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Turks_\(song\) "Young Turks (song)")' — or maybe that other guy with the avian hairdo, [Mike Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Score "Mike Score") from [A Flock of Seagulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Flock_of_Seagulls "A Flock of Seagulls")? And isn't that spooky B-movie [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_\(music\) "Organ (music)") from [Rockwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockwell_\(musician\) "Rockwell (musician)")'s '[Somebody's Watching Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somebody's_Watching_Me "Somebody's Watching Me")'? Abel Tesfaye's [Drambuie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drambuie "Drambuie")\-drenched vocals bathe you in euphoria as you bop around your home in an [N-95](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N95_mask "N95 mask") mask, punching your fist to the 'Hey!-Hey!-Hey!''s, making a magical and much-needed tonic for troubled times".[\[21\]](#cite_note-billboard2020-21)

The genre of the song is generally described as [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music"), [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop"), [synthwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthwave "Synthwave") and [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop"). Audio engineer [Şerban Ghenea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serban_Ghenea "Serban Ghenea") says he loved working on the Weeknd's crisp-sounding "Blinding Lights". "It was crossing two worlds to make something new that fits today, sonically. The older folks like it because it's a throwback, and then the kids love it because it's a new thing that they never heard before."[\[22\]](#cite_note-22)

"Blinding Lights" received universal acclaim from critics.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23)[\[24\]](#cite_note-guardian-24)[\[25\]](#cite_note-nytimes-25)[\[26\]](#cite_note-billboard-26) It was named as the second best song of 2020 by _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ and the best song of 2020 by _[Consequence of Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consequence_of_Sound "Consequence of Sound")_; the former highlighted its nostalgic appeal,[\[27\]](#cite_note-BB100Best2020-27) and the latter praised its "melodic romance waxed over a blockbuster riff".[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")_ magazine named "Blinding Lights" the Record of the Year: "The Weeknd's 'Blinding Lights' is indisputably one of the landmark songs of 2020. The piece has a crystalline synth hook straight out of 1985. The record has come to symbolize strength and triumphing over adversity."[\[29\]](#cite_note-VarietyHitmaker-29) "Blinding Lights" was named one of the best songs of 2019 by _[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")_, where editor Chris DeVille complimented the song's '80s aesthetic and vibe, saying that "the '80s will never die—or, at least, the glamorous neon '80s of our collective imagination".[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

_[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ columnist Kory Grow named "Blinding Lights" as the fourth best song of 2020: "With fuzzy synths and hopscotching [drum-machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_machine "Drum machine") line, 'Blinding Lights' is the best [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music") song this side of [Duran Duran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duran_Duran "Duran Duran"). In just three minutes, the Weeknd checks off any number of Eighties pop-song signposts—unanswered phone calls, driving fast just to feel something, lights representing loneliness—but the real magic is how his voice and the song's chiming [keyboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keyboard_instrument "Keyboard instrument") line lingers in your head well after he injects new life into the greatest Eighties-steeped lyrical cliché of them all: 'I can't sleep until I feel your touch,'" and editor Jon Dolan praised the "[europhile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europhile "Europhile") [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop")\-steeped" production, "Blinding Lights" evokes [Depeche Mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depeche_Mode "Depeche Mode") and [the Human League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Human_League "The Human League") in its lonely-planet luster.[\[4\]](#cite_note-RS-4)[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) David Smyth of _[Evening Standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evening_Standard "Evening Standard")_ also praised the song, calling it a "glorious blast of air punching Eighties synth-pop".[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) Micah Peters from _[The Ringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ringer_\(website\) "The Ringer (website)")_ selected it as one of the best on the album.[\[33\]](#cite_note-Ringer-33) _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ journalist Lindsay Zoladz named "Blinding Lights" one of the best songs of 2020: "It's a propulsive, modernized bit of '80s pastiche. It's always a blessing when the year's most overplayed pop song happens to be one you wouldn't mind hearing a billion and one times anyway," and editor [Jon Caramanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica") added that "'Blinding Lights' is a sterling song that evokes both an idyllic future and triggers aural sense memories of mega-pop's glory years. 'Blinding Lights' could have been lifted from a found [Jazzercise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazzercise "Jazzercise") tape from 1986, though the chilly synths have a slightly sinister tinge \[and\] says a lot about the durability of the Weeknd's early noir—the full commitment to the louche aesthetic he embodied—that even the raging centrist popularity of 'Blinding Lights' can't disinter it."[\[25\]](#cite_note-nytimes-25)[\[34\]](#cite_note-34)[\[35\]](#cite_note-35)

Ben Beaumont-Thomas of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ named "Blinding Lights" one of the best songs of 2020: "It's a titanic pop production from backroom genius Max Martin, who seems to pay homage to his fellow [Scandinavians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scandinavia "Scandinavia") a-ha with the peppy [gated drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gated_drums "Gated drums"). Abel Tesfaye himself shows he can slip between genres casually as he does the lovers in his songs, notching up another wedding [disco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco "Disco") classic."[\[24\]](#cite_note-guardian-24) When describing the Weeknd's ode to '80s music, Nick Levine of [BBC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_News "BBC News") named "Blinding Lights" one of the best songs of 2020: "Co-written and co-produced with Swedish songwriting genius Max Martin, its synth-pop shimmer manages to feel retro and contemporary at the same time—a tricky thing to pull off. Still, the key to its enduring popularity could lie in its ambiguity. Though 'Blinding Lights'' explosive chorus is one of the year's most familiar and uplifting, there's a dash of darkness baked in that keeps things interesting."[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) Editor Makael Wood from _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ named "Blinding Lights" one of the best songs of 2020: "The Weeknd's throwback synth-pop smash was so ubiquitous this year that you couldn't avoid hearing it even when you weren't going anywhere. One aspect that kept it from wearing out its welcome: a crisp tempo just a few ticks faster than you're always expecting."[\[37\]](#cite_note-37)

### Year-end and other lists

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Year-end and other lists")\]

## Grammys controversy

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Grammys controversy")\]

Despite having a successful year in 2020 with the critical and commercial success of "Blinding Lights" and [its parent album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_Hours_\(The_Weeknd_album\) "After Hours (The Weeknd album)"), the Weeknd received zero nominations at the [63rd Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/63rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "63rd Annual Grammy Awards") on November 24, 2020. The gesture spawned much controversy and was a shock to critics, fans, and Tesfaye himself. He responded via social media calling the Grammys "corrupt" in popular social media posts.[\[54\]](#cite_note-54) Speculation arose that the announcement of his upcoming Super Bowl performance, as well as the confusion as to whether he should be nominated as pop or R&B, contributed to the snubs in all the categories that he was submitted to.[\[55\]](#cite_note-55) [Harvey Mason Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Mason_Jr. "Harvey Mason Jr."), interim president of the [Recording Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Academy "Recording Academy"), responded to the backlash by saying:

> We understand that The Weeknd is disappointed at not being nominated. I was surprised and can empathize with what he's feeling. His music this year was excellent, and his contributions to the music community and broader world are worthy of everyone's admiration. We were thrilled when we found out he would be performing at the upcoming Super Bowl and we would have loved to have him also perform on the Grammy stage the weekend before. Unfortunately, every year, there are fewer nominations than the number of deserving artists. But as the only peer-voted music award, we will continue to recognize and celebrate excellence in music while shining a light on the many amazing artists that make up our global community. To be clear, voting in all categories ended well before The Weeknd's performance at the Super Bowl was announced, so in no way could it have affected the nomination process. All Grammy nominees are recognized by the voting body for their excellence, and we congratulate them all.[\[56\]](#cite_note-56)

The Weeknd later made a statement addressing the infamous snub in January 2021, where he said that it felt like "an attack", saying "Look, I personally don't care anymore. I have three GRAMMYs, which mean nothing to me now, obviously...It's not like, 'Oh, I want the GRAMMY!' It's just that this happened, and I'm down to get in front of the fire, as long as it never happens again. I suck at giving speeches anyways. Forget awards shows."[\[57\]](#cite_note-57)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

"Blinding Lights" debuted at number 11 on the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ [Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") on the issue dated December 14, 2019,[\[80\]](#cite_note-cbc082021-81) but fell 41 places to number 52 in its second week.[\[81\]](#cite_note-82) In its 12th week on the chart, the song became the Weeknd's tenth top ten hit by rising to a new peak at number ten.[\[82\]](#cite_note-83) On the issue dated Mar

"**Blinding Lights**" is a song by Canadian singer-songwriter [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd"), from his fourth studio album, _[After Hours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_Hours_\(The_Weeknd_album\) "After Hours (The Weeknd album)")_ (2020).
