It was written by the Weeknd, [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin"), [Oscar Holter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Holter "Oscar Holter"), [Belly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belly_\(rapper\) "Belly (rapper)"), and [DaHeala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DaHeala "DaHeala"), while being produced by the former three.

"Blinding Lights" received universal acclaim by music journalists upon release, with many noting its aesthetic, as well as its callback to the [music of the 1980s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_the_1980s "Music of the 1980s"). The song was a commercial success, topping the record charts in over 40 countries, including his native Canada, making it his most successful single to date. In the United States, "Blinding Lights" topped the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") for four non-consecutive weeks, earning his fifth number one in the country. It became the song with the [most weeks spent in the top five and top ten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") and the first song to hold a spot in the top ten for an entire year.

It was the [longest-charting song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_total_weeks_on_the_Hot_100 "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") in history for a short period of time, remaining on it for a total of 90 weeks, and was named as the chart's [best-performing song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#All-time_achievements "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") of all time on November 23, 2021. It was certified diamond by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) and seven times platinum by the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") (BPI). According to the [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry"), it was the [best-selling global single of 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles#Best-selling_singles_by_year_worldwide "List of best-selling singles") and the best-selling song overall since 2020 by stream equivalent units. On [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), it is the [most streamed song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records#Most-streamed_songs "List of Spotify streaming records") of all time, and the first song to surpass four and five billion streams.

Anton Tammi directed the song's music video, which was filmed over a four-day period shot in the night. Inspired by films such as _[Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear_and_Loathing_in_Las_Vegas_\(film\) "Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas (film)")_ (1998), _[Joker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joker_\(2019_film\) "Joker (2019 film)")_ (2019), and _[Casino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casino_\(1995_film\) "Casino (1995 film)")_ (1995), it depicts the Weeknd speeding through a city, after getting beaten by bouncers and being forced on the run. "Blinding Lights" was performed on television shows such as _[The Late Show with Stephen Colbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Late_Show_with_Stephen_Colbert "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert")_, _[Jimmy Kimmel Live!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Kimmel_Live! "Jimmy Kimmel Live!")_, _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")_, his headlining set at the [Super Bowl LV halftime show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LV_halftime_show "Super Bowl LV halftime show"), and was included on the set list for his [After Hours til Dawn Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_Hours_til_Dawn_Tour "After Hours til Dawn Tour"). It received several awards and nominations, winning Song of the Year at the [2021 iHeartRadio Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_iHeartRadio_Music_Awards "2021 iHeartRadio Music Awards") and [Juno Awards of 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Awards_of_2021 "Juno Awards of 2021").

## Background and development

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and development")\]

In November 2018, [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") announced at a concert that he was working on his fourth studio album, tentatively referred to as "Chapter VI".[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

After a five-month social media hiatus, the singer-songwriter returned to [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") on November 20, 2019, and posted six days later on November 26, 2019.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) He previously announced a project referred to as _Chapter VI_ in June 2019.[\[9\]](#cite_note-nme-9) On November 24, 2019, a [Mercedes-Benz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz "Mercedes-Benz") commercial first aired on German TV featuring a clip of "Blinding Lights".[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) It shows the Weeknd driving a [Mercedes-Benz EQC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_EQC "Mercedes-Benz EQC") SUV and asking the system to play his new song.[\[12\]](#cite_note-rap-up-12) The full-length version of the commercial premiered on November 29, alongside the single.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) In the days after, he took to social media to announce his return to music with the captions "the fall starts tomorrow night" and "Tonight we start a new brain melting psychotic chapter! Let's go!"[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

During an interview conducted by Jem Aswad from _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")_ magazine, the Weeknd discussed his experience working with Swedish songwriter-producer [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin"), saying: "Max and I have become literally the best of friends, but I don't do that with many people. It's not that I can't, but a collaboration is a relationship, it's like a marriage, you've gotta build up to it."[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) In a _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ interview, the Weeknd expressed his appreciation for [music of the 1980s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980s_in_music "1980s in music"): "I've always had an admiration for the era before I was born. You can hear it as far back as my [first mixtape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Balloons "House of Balloons") that the '80s — [Siouxsie and the Banshees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouxsie_and_the_Banshees "Siouxsie and the Banshees"), [Cocteau Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocteau_Twins "Cocteau Twins") — play such a huge role in my sound. Sometimes it helps me create a new sound and sometimes it's just obvious. I'm just glad the world's into it now."[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) In an interview with _[Vanity Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity_Fair_\(magazine\) "Vanity Fair (magazine)")_, the Weeknd said that he initially thought that the song would be a commercial failure.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

## Lyrics and composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Lyrics and composition")\]

Throughout the song, the Weeknd sings about the rekindling of a relationship and the importance of his partner. He also mentions the city of [Las Vegas, Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas,_Nevada "Las Vegas, Nevada"), when he refers to it by its nickname "Sin City" in the [pre-chorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-chorus "Pre-chorus").[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) In a profile in [_Esquire_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esquire_\(magazine\) "Esquire (magazine)"), The Weeknd explained that "'Blinding Lights' \[is about\] how you want to see someone at night, and you're intoxicated, and you're driving to this person and you're just blinded by streetlights, but nothing could stop you from trying to go see that person, because you're so lonely. I don't want to ever promote drunk driving, but that's what the dark undertone is."[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

From its scale-laddering verses to its tension-filled chorus, the song exhibits the polish and "melodic math" for which [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin") is renowned, according to Chris Molanphy from _[Slate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slate_\(magazine\) "Slate (magazine)")_.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) The [Dorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorian_mode "Dorian mode") structure provides a dreamy and euphoric nature to the song while still ultimately resolving to a minor chord. Exclusively in the music video, the song temporarily modulates to E♭ Dorian as the [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute") drops for 3 and a half measures.

_[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ staff writer Frank DiGiacomo assessed its qualities, "The opening drumbeat is a [DeLorean \[time machine\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeLorean_time_machine "DeLorean time machine") [back to](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_to_the_Future "Back to the Future") [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson")'s '[Beat It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beat_It "Beat It")'. The [amphetamine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphetamine "Amphetamine") [synth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer "Synthesizer") conjures fond memories of leopard-print-era [Rod Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_Stewart "Rod Stewart")'s '[Young Turks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Turks_\(song\) "Young Turks (song)")' — or maybe that other guy with the avian hairdo, [Mike Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Score "Mike Score") from [A Flock of Seagulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Flock_of_Seagulls "A Flock of Seagulls")? And isn't that spooky B-movie [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_\(music\) "Organ (music)") from [Rockwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockwell_\(musician\) "Rockwell (musician)")'s '[Somebody's Watching Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somebody's_Watching_Me "Somebody's Watching Me")'? Abel Tesfaye's [Drambuie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drambuie "Drambuie")\-drenched vocals bathe you in euphoria as you bop around your home in an [N-95](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N95_mask "N95 mask") mask, punching your fist to the 'Hey!-Hey!-Hey!''s, making a magical and much-needed tonic for troubled times".[\[21\]](#cite_note-billboard2020-21)

The genre of the song is generally described as [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music"), [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop"), [synthwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthwave "Synthwave") and [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop"). Audio engineer [Şerban Ghenea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serban_Ghenea "Serban Ghenea") says he loved working on the Weeknd's crisp-sounding "Blinding Lights". "It was crossing two worlds to make something new that fits today, sonically. The older folks like it because it's a throwback, and then the kids love it because it's a new thing that they never heard before."[\[22\]](#cite_note-22)

"Blinding Lights" received universal acclaim from critics.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23)[\[24\]](#cite_note-guardian-24)[\[25\]](#cite_note-nytimes-25)[\[26\]](#cite_note-billboard-26) It was named as the second best song of 2020 by _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ and the best song of 2020 by _[Consequence of Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consequence_of_Sound "Consequence of Sound")_; the former highlighted its nostalgic appeal,[\[27\]](#cite_note-BB100Best2020-27) and the latter praised its "melodic romance waxed over a blockbuster riff".[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")_ magazine named "Blinding Lights" the Record of the Year: "The Weeknd's 'Blinding Lights' is indisputably one of the landmark songs of 2020. The piece has a crystalline synth hook straight out of 1985. The record has come to symbolize strength and triumphing over adversity."[\[29\]](#cite_note-VarietyHitmaker-29) "Blinding Lights" was named one of the best songs of 2019 by _[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")_, where editor Chris DeVille complimented the song's '80s aesthetic and vibe, saying that "the '80s will never die—or, at least, the glamorous neon '80s of our collective imagination".[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

_[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ columnist Kory Grow named "Blinding Lights" as the fourth best song of 2020: "With fuzzy synths and hopscotching [drum-machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_machine "Drum machine") line, 'Blinding Lights' is the best [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music") song this side of [Duran Duran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duran_Duran "Duran Duran"). In just three minutes, the Weeknd checks off any number of Eighties pop-song signposts—unanswered phone calls, driving fast just to feel something, lights representing loneliness—but the real magic is how his voice and the song's chiming [keyboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keyboard_instrument "Keyboard instrument") line lingers in your head well after he injects new life into the greatest Eighties-steeped lyrical cliché of them all: 'I can't sleep until I feel your touch,'" and editor Jon Dolan praised the "[europhile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europhile "Europhile") [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop")\-steeped" production, "Blinding Lights" evokes [Depeche Mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depeche_Mode "Depeche Mode") and [the Human League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Human_League "The Human League") in its lonely-planet luster.[\[4\]](#cite_note-RS-4)[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) David Smyth of _[Evening Standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evening_Standard "Evening Standard")_ also praised the song, calling it a "glorious blast of air punching Eighties synth-pop".[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) Micah Peters from _[The Ringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ringer_\(website\) "The Ringer (website)")_ selected it as one of the best on the album.[\[33\]](#cite_note-Ringer-33) _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ journalist Lindsay Zoladz named "Blinding Lights" one of the best songs of 2020: "It's a propulsive, modernized bit of '80s pastiche. It's always a blessing when the year's most overplayed pop song happens to be one you wouldn't mind hearing a billion and one times anyway," and editor [Jon Caramanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica") added that "'Blinding Lights' is a sterling song that evokes both an idyllic future and triggers aural sense memories of mega-pop's glory years. 'Blinding Lights' could have been lifted from a found [Jazzercise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazzercise "Jazzercise") tape from 1986, though the chilly synths have a slightly sinister tinge \[and\] says a lot about the durability of the Weeknd's early noir—the full commitment to the louche aesthetic he embodied—that even the raging centrist popularity of 'Blinding Lights' can't disinter it."[\[25\]](#cite_note-nytimes-25)[\[34\]](#cite_note-34)[\[35\]](#cite_note-35)

Ben Beaumont-Thomas of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ named "Blinding Lights" one of the best songs of 2020: "It's a titanic pop production from backroom genius Max Martin, who seems to pay homage to his fellow [Scandinavians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scandinavia "Scandinavia") a-ha with the peppy [gated drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gated_drums "Gated drums"). Abel Tesfaye himself shows he can slip between genres casually as he does the lovers in his songs, notching up another wedding [disco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco "Disco") classic."[\[24\]](#cite_note-guardian-24) When describing the Weeknd's ode to '80s music, Nick Levine of [BBC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_News "BBC News") named "Blinding Lights" one of the best songs of 2020: "Co-written and co-produced with Swedish songwriting genius Max Martin, its synth-pop shimmer manages to feel retro and contemporary at the same time—a tricky thing to pull off. Still, the key to its enduring popularity could lie in its ambiguity. Though 'Blinding Lights'' explosive chorus is one of the year's most familiar and uplifting, there's a dash of darkness baked in that keeps things interesting."[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) Editor Makael Wood from _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ named "Blinding Lights" one of the best songs of 2020: "The Weeknd's throwback synth-pop smash was so ubiquitous this year that you couldn't avoid hearing it even when you weren't going anywhere. One aspect that kept it from wearing out its welcome: a crisp tempo just a few ticks faster than you're always expecting."[\[37\]](#cite_note-37)

### Year-end and other lists

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Year-end and other lists")\]

## Grammys controversy

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Grammys controversy")\]

Despite having a successful year in 2020 with the critical and commercial success of "Blinding Lights" and [its parent album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_Hours_\(The_Weeknd_album\) "After Hours (The Weeknd album)"), the Weeknd received zero nominations at the [63rd Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/63rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "63rd Annual Grammy Awards") on November 24, 2020. The gesture spawned much controversy and was a shock to critics, fans, and Tesfaye himself. He responded via social media calling the Grammys "corrupt" in popular social media posts.[\[54\]](#cite_note-54) Speculation arose that the announcement of his upcoming Super Bowl performance, as well as the confusion as to whether he should be nominated as pop or R&B, contributed to the snubs in all the categories that he was submitted to.[\[55\]](#cite_note-55) [Harvey Mason Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Mason_Jr. "Harvey Mason Jr."), interim president of the [Recording Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Academy "Recording Academy"), responded to the backlash by saying:

> We understand that The Weeknd is disappointed at not being nominated. I was surprised and can empathize with what he's feeling. His music this year was excellent, and his contributions to the music community and broader world are worthy of everyone's admiration. We were thrilled when we found out he would be performing at the upcoming Super Bowl and we would have loved to have him also perform on the Grammy stage the weekend before. Unfortunately, every year, there are fewer nominations than the number of deserving artists. But as the only peer-voted music award, we will continue to recognize and celebrate excellence in music while shining a light on the many amazing artists that make up our global community. To be clear, voting in all categories ended well before The Weeknd's performance at the Super Bowl was announced, so in no way could it have affected the nomination process. All Grammy nominees are recognized by the voting body for their excellence, and we congratulate them all.[\[56\]](#cite_note-56)

The Weeknd later made a statement addressing the infamous snub in January 2021, where he said that it felt like "an attack", saying "Look, I personally don't care anymore. I have three GRAMMYs, which mean nothing to me now, obviously...It's not like, 'Oh, I want the GRAMMY!' It's just that this happened, and I'm down to get in front of the fire, as long as it never happens again. I suck at giving speeches anyways. Forget awards shows."[\[57\]](#cite_note-57)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

"Blinding Lights" debuted at number 11 on the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ [Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") on the issue dated December 14, 2019,[\[80\]](#cite_note-cbc082021-81) but fell 41 places to number 52 in its second week.[\[81\]](#cite_note-82) In its 12th week on the chart, the song became the Weeknd's tenth top ten hit by rising to a new peak at number ten.[\[82\]](#cite_note-83) On the issue dated Mar

# Die for You

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

**Die for You** may refer to:

*   [_Die for You_ (album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die_for_You_\(album\) "Die for You (album)"), by Antique, 2001

"**Die for You**" is a song by the Canadian singer-songwriter [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd"), from his third studio album, _[Starboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(album\) "Starboy (album)")_ (2016). The song was sent to US [rhythmic contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_contemporary "Rhythmic contemporary") radio on September 19, 2017, as the seventh single from the album. It was written by the Weeknd, [Doc McKinney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_McKinney "Doc McKinney"), [Cirkut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirkut "Cirkut"), Prince 85, [Cashmere Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cashmere_Cat "Cashmere Cat"), [Dylan Wiggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Wiggins "Dylan Wiggins"), and Billy Walsh, and produced by the former five.

The song was initially a moderate success, achieving a peak within the top 50 of the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). In 2022, the song experienced a resurgence in popularity due to the online social media application [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok"). The song thereafter impacted US [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") and peaked at number six on the Hot 100. On February 24, 2023, the Weeknd released a remix of "Die for You" with American singer-songwriter [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande"), which was included on the deluxe edition of _Starboy_. The remix propelled the song to number one on the Hot 100, marking both artists' seventh number-one single on the chart, following both artists' sixth, the remix of "[Save Your Tears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_Your_Tears "Save Your Tears")" (2021). The remix also reached a new peak at number two on the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") and the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"). According to the [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry") (IFPI), the remix was the fourth best-selling global single of 2023, earning 1.78 billion subscription streams equivalents globally.

## Background and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Die_for_You_\(The_Weeknd_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

In a 2016 interview with Zane Lowe of Beats 1 Radio, the Weeknd said that "Die for You" was the last song to finish for his album _Starboy_ and was completed merely a week before the album dropped.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) It was one of the tracks on the album to be previewed before its release as part of the 12-minute-long short film _Mania_, released on November 23.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) The song was officially released on November 25, 2016, as an album track.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

"Die for You" received early airplay from [urban contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_contemporary "Urban contemporary") and [urban adult contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_adult_contemporary "Urban adult contemporary") radio in August 2017.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) It was officially serviced to US [rhythmic contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_contemporary "Rhythmic contemporary") radio on September 19, 2017, as the sixth single from _Starboy_ in the United States.[\[7\]](#cite_note-single_release_date-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) The song was also scheduled to be sent to US [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") on December 5, but its release to the format in the country was cancelled for unknown reasons.[\[9\]](#cite_note-Cancelled_pop_radio_release_date-9) Following its release as a single in North America, the song charted modestly across various _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ component charts and became a moderate Canadian hit. "Die for You" would later then be included on the track list of the Weeknd's second [greatest hits album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_hits_album "Greatest hits album"), _[The Highlights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Highlights "The Highlights")_, which was released on February 5, 2021.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

After a resurgence in popularity due to increased usage on the video-sharing app [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok") in September 2021, its official music video was released on November 25, 2021, alongside standalone digital release on Apple Music with its own artwork.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) As a result, the song would begin receiving [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") airplay in early August 2022, following its initial cancellation from the release in 2017.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) In February 2023, the Weeknd uploaded a live performance video of the song from his [After Hours til Dawn Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_Hours_til_Dawn_Tour "After Hours til Dawn Tour") to promote his [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") concert special _the Weeknd: Live at SoFi Stadium_.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) A live version of the song from his performance at [SoFi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoFi_Stadium "SoFi Stadium") was later released to digital stores and streaming platforms in March 2023 with the release of his first live album _[Live at SoFi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_at_SoFi_Stadium "Live at SoFi Stadium")_.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

## Composition and lyrics

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Die_for_You_\(The_Weeknd_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition and lyrics")\]

The song's sheet music, published by Sony/ATV Music Publishing at musicnotes.com, shows that "Die for You" is written in the key of [C♯ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-sharp_minor "C-sharp minor") and follows a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 72 beats per minute. The vocals in the song span from the low note of C♯4 to the high note of C♯6.[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

In an interview with [Zane Lowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zane_Lowe "Zane Lowe"), the Weeknd stated that "Die for You" was the final song finished for _Starboy_, and that it was difficult to write, specifically its lyrics.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

Mosi Reeves of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ said that the song "is a euphoric slow jam where he finally summons the poetic sincerity he mined so easily in the past."[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) [Christopher Hooton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Hooton "Christopher Hooton") of _[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")_ said that the song "has a tragic ecstasy to it befitting an end of the world party that happens to fall on New Years' Eve."[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) Larry Bartleet of _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ called it "banal, forgettable fluff".[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Die_for_You_\(The_Weeknd_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

In the United States, "Die for You" peaked at number 43 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and charted for three weeks during its original run. Additionally, the song reached number 19 on the [Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs") chart. In Canada, the song peaked at number 35 on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100") and charted for 20 weeks.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

In late 2021 and throughout 2022, "Die for You" saw an increase in consumption as the song went viral on the social media platform [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok") alongside fellow album track "[Stargirl Interlude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargirl_Interlude "Stargirl Interlude")".[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) This increase in streaming and sales led to the song's parent album to re-enter the top 40 on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") chart.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) It also led to the song entering the top 40 of multiple single charts across Asia and Oceania, with the song additionally reaching number 19 on the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") chart and re-entering the _Billboard_ Hot 100, peaking at number six.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) On February 6, 2023, "Die for You" topped the US [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart, over six years after its arrival on _Starboy_. On the same day, it also reached number one on the mainstream top 40-based US [Pop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Airplay "Pop Airplay") chart. On both charts, "Die for You" stayed at the top for two weeks.[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)

"Die for You" was featured in the second season of the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy-drama television series _[Insecure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insecure_\(TV_series\) "Insecure (TV series)")_.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27)[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) Due to its appearance in the show, the song led the THR's Top TV Songs Chart in August 2017.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29)

"**Die for You**" is a song by the Canadian singer-songwriter [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd"), from his third studio album, _[Starboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(album\) "Starboy (album)")_ (2016). The song was sent to US [rhythmic contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_contemporary "Rhythmic contemporary") radio on September 19, 2017, as the seventh single from the album. It was written by the Weeknd, [Doc McKinney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_McKinney "Doc McKinney"), [Cirkut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirkut "Cirkut"), Prince 85, [Cashmere Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cashmere_Cat "Cashmere Cat"), [Dylan Wiggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Wiggins "Dylan Wiggins"), and Billy Walsh, and produced by the former five.

The song was initially a moderate success, achieving a peak within the top 50 of the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). In 2022, the song experienced a resurgence in popularity due to the online social media application [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok"). The song thereafter impacted US [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") and peaked at number six on the Hot 100. On February 24, 2023, the Weeknd released a remix of "Die for You" with American singer-songwriter [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande"), which was included on the deluxe edition of _Starboy_. The remix propelled the song to number one on the Hot 100, marking both artists' seventh number-one single on the chart, following both artists' sixth, the remix of "[Save Your Tears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_Your_Tears "Save Your Tears")" (2021). The remix also reached a new peak at number two on the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") and the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"). According to the [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry") (IFPI), the remix was the fourth best-selling global single of 2023, earning 1.78 billion subscription streams equivalents globally.

## Background and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Die_for_You_\(The_Weeknd_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

In a 2016 interview with Zane Lowe of Beats 1 Radio, the Weeknd said that "Die for You" was the last song to finish for his album _Starboy_ and was completed merely a week before the album dropped.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) It was one of the tracks on the album to be previewed before its release as part of the 12-minute-long short film _Mania_, released on November 23.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) The song was officially released on November 25, 2016, as an album track.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

"Die for You" received early airplay from [urban contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_contemporary "Urban contemporary") and [urban adult contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_adult_contemporary "Urban adult contemporary") radio in August 2017.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) It was officially serviced to US [rhythmic contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_contemporary "Rhythmic contemporary") radio on September 19, 2017, as the sixth single from _Starboy_ in the United States.[\[7\]](#cite_note-single_release_date-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) The song was also scheduled to be sent to US [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") on December 5, but its release to the format in the country was cancelled for unknown reasons.[\[9\]](#cite_note-Cancelled_pop_radio_release_date-9) Following its release as a single in North America, the song charted modestly across various _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ component charts and became a moderate Canadian hit. "Die for You" would later then be included on the track list of the Weeknd's second [greatest hits album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_hits_album "Greatest hits album"), _[The Highlights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Highlights "The Highlights")_, which was released on February 5, 2021.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

After a resurgence in popularity due to increased usage on the video-sharing app [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok") in September 2021, its official music video was released on November 25, 2021, alongside standalone digital release on Apple Music with its own artwork.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) As a result, the song would begin receiving [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") airplay in early August 2022, following its initial cancellation from the release in 2017.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) In February 2023, the Weeknd uploaded a live performance video of the song from his [After Hours til Dawn Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_Hours_til_Dawn_Tour "After Hours til Dawn Tour") to promote his [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") concert special _the Weeknd: Live at SoFi Stadium_.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) A live version of the song from his performance at [SoFi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoFi_Stadium "SoFi Stadium") was later released to digital stores and streaming platforms in March 2023 with the release of his first live album _[Live at SoFi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_at_SoFi_Stadium "Live at SoFi Stadium")_.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

## Composition and lyrics

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Die_for_You_\(The_Weeknd_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition and lyrics")\]

The song's sheet music, published by Sony/ATV Music Publishing at musicnotes.com, shows that "Die for You" is written in the key of [C♯ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-sharp_minor "C-sharp minor") and follows a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 72 beats per minute. The vocals in the song span from the low note of C♯4 to the high note of C♯6.[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

In an interview with [Zane Lowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zane_Lowe "Zane Lowe"), the Weeknd stated that "Die for You" was the final song finished for _Starboy_, and that it was difficult to write, specifically its lyrics.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

Mosi Reeves of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ said that the song "is a euphoric slow jam where he finally summons the poetic sincerity he mined so easily in the past."[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) [Christopher Hooton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Hooton "Christopher Hooton") of _[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")_ said that the song "has a tragic ecstasy to it befitting an end of the world party that happens to fall on New Years' Eve."[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) Larry Bartleet of _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ called it "banal, forgettable fluff".[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Die_for_You_\(The_Weeknd_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

In the United States, "Die for You" peaked at number 43 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and charted for three weeks during its original run. Additionally, the song reached number 19 on the [Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs") chart. In Canada, the song peaked at number 35 on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100") and charted for 20 weeks.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

In late 2021 and throughout 2022, "Die for You" saw an increase in consumption as the song went viral on the social media platform [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok") alongside fellow album track "[Stargirl Interlude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargirl_Interlude "Stargirl Interlude")".[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) This increase in streaming and sales led to the song's parent album to re-enter the top 40 on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") chart.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) It also led to the song entering the top 40 of multiple single charts across Asia and Oceania, with the song additionally reaching number 19 on the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") chart and re-entering the _Billboard_ Hot 100, peaking at number six.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) On February 6, 2023, "Die for You" topped the US [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart, over six years after its arrival on _Starboy_. On the same day, it also reached number one on the mainstream top 40-based US [Pop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Airplay "Pop Airplay") chart. On both charts, "Die for You" stayed at the top for two weeks.[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)

"Die for You" was featured in the second season of the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy-drama television series _[Insecure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insecure_\(TV_series\) "Insecure (TV series)")_.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27)[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) Due to its appearance in the show, the song led the THR's Top TV Songs Chart in August 2017.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29)

On November 25, 2021, to celebrate the five-year anniversary of _Starboy_'s release, the Weeknd surprise-released the music video for "Die for You", directed by [Christian Breslauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Breslauer "Christian Breslauer").[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

The video pays [homage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homage_\(arts\) "Homage (arts)") to the [science fiction horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_films "Horror films") television series _[Stranger Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stranger_Things "Stranger Things")_ (2016-2025) and the [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction "Science fiction") film _[E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.T._the_Extra-Terrestrial "E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial")_ (1982).[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) It follows a boy who hides in a house and is discovered by a girl living in the same house. # Blinding Lights

ch 28, 2020, the song rose two places to reach number two.[\[83\]](#cite_note-84) The song reached number one on [R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs "R&B/Hip-Hop Songs") on April 4, 2020, leading for 11 non-consecutive weeks.[\[84\]](#cite_note-Trust-85) The song also reached number one on [R&B Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R&B_Songs "R&B Songs") chart on March 7, 2020, where it became his seventh number one on the chart, making him the artist with the most number ones on the chart's history and also attaining a record-breaking reign of 48 weeks.[\[85\]](#cite_note-86) On March 30, 2020, the song rose to number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, dethroning [Roddy Ricch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roddy_Ricch "Roddy Ricch")'s "[The Box](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Box_\(Roddy_Ricch_song\) "The Box (Roddy Ricch song)")" on the issue dated April 4, 2020.[\[86\]](#cite_note-BH100_Peak-87) The single kept at its peak position the following week, becoming the Weeknd's third multi-week leader after "[The Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hills_\(song\) "The Hills (song)")", which topped the chart five years earlier.[\[87\]](#cite_note-88) "Blinding Lights" spent four weeks atop the Hot 100 and finished 2020 as the [year's top _Billboard_ Hot 100 song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2020 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2020").[\[88\]](#cite_note-BBNo1OfYear-89) The following year, it ranked at number three on the year-end chart, becoming the first single to finish in the top three on two occasions.[\[89\]](#cite_note-90)

"Blinding Lights" spent 57 weeks in the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and 43 weeks in the top five, breaking the record for the most time logged in the region over the chart's 62-year history.[\[90\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-91)[\[91\]](#cite_note-BillboardUSCert-92) On the [Digital Song Sales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Songs "Digital Songs") chart, the song peaked at number one for the week of March 23, 2020, and became the Weeknd's fifth Digital Songs number one. The single reached a peak of number one on the [Streaming Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_Songs "Streaming Songs") chart on March 30, becoming his first topper on the listing since "The Hills" led five years earlier.[\[92\]](#cite_note-93) On April 13, the song reached number one on [Pop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Songs "Pop Songs") chart, where it led for 6 non-consecutive weeks, as it slid to number two on the Hot 100.[\[93\]](#cite_note-94) It later rose back up to number one for the two following weeks.[\[94\]](#cite_note-95)[\[95\]](#cite_note-BB4thweek-96)[\[96\]](#cite_note-97) On May 18, the song became his first number one on the [Adult Pop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Pop_Songs "Adult Pop Songs") chart, leading for 20 non-consecutive weeks.[\[97\]](#cite_note-98) On November 7, "Blinding Lights" became his first number one on the [Adult Contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_\(chart\) "Adult Contemporary (chart)") chart, where it led for 35 non-consecutive weeks.[\[98\]](#cite_note-99)[\[99\]](#cite_note-100) "Blinding Lights" topped [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") for a record-breaking 26 weeks, passing [Goo Goo Dolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goo_Goo_Dolls "Goo Goo Dolls")' "[Iris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_\(song\) "Iris (song)")", which held the record as the longest-running chart-topper for almost 22 years.[\[100\]](#cite_note-101) [\[101\]](#cite_note-102) "Blinding Lights" fell out of the Hot 100 for the week dated January 2, 2021, but it re-entered at number 3 the next week, breaking the three-way tie for the highest song to re-enter the Hot 100.[\[102\]](#cite_note-103)[\[103\]](#cite_note-104) Meanwhile, "Blinding Lights" tied for the most time totaled in the Hot 100's top three, 21 weeks, equaling the sums of The [Chainsmokers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chainsmokers "Chainsmokers")' "[Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Closer (The Chainsmokers song)")" and [Mark Ronson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Ronson "Mark Ronson")'s "[Uptown Funk!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uptown_Funk "Uptown Funk")".[\[90\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-91)

For a short time during 2022, "Blinding Lights" was the longest running single in the history of the Hot 100 chart with a total of 90 weeks, surpassing [Imagine Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imagine_Dragons "Imagine Dragons")' "[Radioactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Radioactive (Imagine Dragons song)")", which spent 87 weeks.[\[80\]](#cite_note-cbc082021-81)[\[104\]](#cite_note-105) In the process, the song also attained the longest chart run of any Hot 100 chart-topper in _Billboard_ history, surpassing the 68-week run by [LMFAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMFAO "LMFAO")'s "[Party Rock Anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Rock_Anthem "Party Rock Anthem")" (2011–12).[\[105\]](#cite_note-106) On November 23, 2021, the song surpassed "[The Twist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twist_\(song\) "The Twist (song)")" (1960) as the [number-one song of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Top_10_songs_of_all_time_\(1958–2021\) "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") in _Billboard_ Hot 100 history.[\[106\]](#cite_note-BBNo1AllTime-107) On April 5, 2022, "Blinding Lights" was awarded a [Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") certification from the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) for selling ten million units in the United States.[\[91\]](#cite_note-BillboardUSCert-92)

"Blinding Lights" also became producer Max Martin's 23rd Hot 100 number one single as a writer, 21st as producer, and his first in both credits since [Justin Timberlake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Timberlake "Justin Timberlake")'s "[Can't Stop the Feeling!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Stop_the_Feeling! "Can't Stop the Feeling!")" (2016). Martin has the third-most as writer, behind [Paul McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney") (32) and [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") (26), and the second-most as producer, behind [George Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Martin "George Martin") (23).[\[86\]](#cite_note-BH100_Peak-87) The Weeknd became the first artist to simultaneously lead _Billboard_'s five primary charts on March 30, topping the Hot 100, [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), [Artist 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artist_100 "Artist 100"), Hot 100 Songwriters and Hot 100 Producers.[\[107\]](#cite_note-108)[\[108\]](#cite_note-109) The next week, he topped the Hot 100, Billboard 200 and Artist 100 once more, achieving the feat for a fourth time.[\[109\]](#cite_note-110)

On the [_Rolling Stone_ Top 100 Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone_Top_100 "Rolling Stone Top 100") chart, the song debuted at number two, where it was blocked from the top spot by the Weeknd's own "[Heartless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartless_\(The_Weeknd_song\) "Heartless (The Weeknd song)")". The song also became the Weeknd's second entry on the chart.[\[110\]](#cite_note-111) It later rose to number one on the chart following the release of _After Hours_.[\[111\]](#cite_note-RS6Months-112)

In the singer's native Canada, "Blinding Lights" debuted at number two on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), one place higher than "Heartless". It later managed to reach number one after the release of its parent album on the issue dated April 4, 2020, becoming the Weeknd's fifth number-one single in the country. It spent seven weeks atop the chart, tying "[Starboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(song\) "Starboy (song)")" as his longest-running chart-topper.[\[112\]](#cite_note-113) In May 2021, "Blinding Lights" dropped off the Canadian Hot 100 after 75 weeks on the chart,[\[113\]](#cite_note-114) leaving it one week short of the all-time record set by "[I Gotta Feeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Gotta_Feeling "I Gotta Feeling")" by the [Black Eyed Peas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Eyed_Peas "Black Eyed Peas") in 2010.[\[114\]](#cite_note-115) For the first half of 2020, "Blinding Lights" was the top Canadian song overall, with 484,000 units.[\[115\]](#cite_note-116) It has been certified Diamond by [Music Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Canada "Music Canada") for selling 800,000 units.[\[116\]](#cite_note-117)

### Europe, Oceania and Latin America

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Europe, Oceania and Latin America")\]

In the United Kingdom,"Blinding Lights" debuted at number 12 on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") on December 6, 2019 – for the week ending date December 12, 2019. It eventually peaked at the top of the chart in February 2020, becoming the Weeknd's first number-one single in Britain.[\[117\]](#cite_note-118) After two weeks at number one, it dropped a place number two. However it rebounded to number one the week after, and remained there for three consecutive weeks. The week after it fell a place to number two and also stayed at the runner-up spot for another week. The following week, it once again rebounded to number one, and stayed there for another three consecutive weeks. Overall, the single spent eight non-consecutive weeks atop the singles chart.[\[118\]](#cite_note-OfficialScores-119)[\[119\]](#cite_note-120) It dropped to number two on April 24, 2020 – for the week ending April 30, 2020 – after the Weeknd used [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") to ask people to support its close rival, a charity single, "[You'll Never Walk Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You'll_Never_Walk_Alone#Michael_Ball_&_Captain_Tom_Moore_version "You'll Never Walk Alone")", by [Michael Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Ball "Michael Ball") and [Captain Sir Tom Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_Tom_Moore "Captain Tom Moore"), and make it number one for Moore's 100th birthday.[\[120\]](#cite_note-Jones-121)[\[121\]](#cite_note-122) As a result, "Blinding Lights" dropped a place to number two and remained at number two the following week, behind another charity single, "[Times Like These](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Like_These_\(Foo_Fighters_song\)#Live_Lounge_Allstars_charity_single "Times Like These (Foo Fighters song)")".[\[122\]](#cite_note-OC-123)[\[123\]](#cite_note-OC2-124) According to the [Official Charts Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Charts_Company "Official Charts Company"), "Blinding Lights" became Britain's biggest-selling song of 2020 with 2.2 million combined sales, including 250 million streams and 195,000 downloads.[\[124\]](#cite_note-UKbiggest-125) "Blinding Lights" has been certified 6× Platinum by the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") for selling 3,600,000 units.[\[125\]](#cite_note-126)

Elsewhere in Europe, the song topped the charts in Austria, Belgium, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, the Republic of Ireland, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Sweden, and Switzerland. It also peaked within the top ten of the charts in Belarus, Hungary, Malta, North Macedonia, Russia, Romania, Spain, and Ukraine.

In Australia, it topped the [ARIA Charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts") for eleven non-consecutive weeks. It is the sixth longest-running number-one of all-time in the country, tied with songs such as [Spice Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spice_Girls "Spice Girls")'s "[Wannabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wannabe "Wannabe")", [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)")'s "[God's Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God's_Plan_\(song\) "God's Plan (song)")" and [Bryan Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Adams "Bryan Adams")' "[(Everything I Do) I Do It for You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/\(Everything_I_Do\)_I_Do_It_for_You "(Everything I Do) I Do It for You")", as well the fifth longest by a foreign act.[\[126\]](#cite_note-AriaReturns-127) "Blinding Lights" has been certified 13× Platinum by the [Australian Recording Industry Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Recording_Industry_Association "Australian Recording Industry Association") for selling 910,000 units.[\[127\]](#cite_note-128)

In New Zealand, the song topped the [New Zealand Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Singles_Chart "New Zealand Singles Chart") for four non-consecutive weeks.

In Latin America, "Blinding Lights" topped the charts in Bolivia and Mexico. It also reached the top 10 in Chile, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Honduras, Panama, Puerto Rico and Uruguay, as well as the top 20 in Argentina, Nicaragua, Paraguay and Peru. It also charted in Brazil and Colombia, peaking at numbers 51 and 66 respectively.

"Blinding Lights" was the [best-selling global single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles "List of best-selling singles") of 2020, earning 2.72 billion subscription stream equivalents globally. For this feat, it was awarded the IFPI Global Digital Single Award by the [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry") (IFPI).[\[128\]](#cite_note-IFPI-129) It was also the seventh best-selling global single of 2021 with 1.61 billion subscription stream equivalents globally[\[129\]](#cite_note-IFPI2-130) and the fourteenth best-selling global single of 2022 with 1.01 billion subscription stream equivalents globally.[\[130\]](#cite_note-IFPI3-131)

"Blinding Lights" has also broken numerous records on streaming platform [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"). It was the most-streamed song of 2020 on the platform with nearly 1.6 billion streams.[\[131\]](#cite_note-132) On February 24, 2021, it became the first song by a Canadian artist and only the fourth song in history to pass two billion plays on the platform;[\[132\]](#cite_note-133) it also broke the record for the fastest song to do so, in under 15 months.[\[133\]](#cite_note-134) On June 15, 2022, it became the first song by a Canadian artist and only the second song in history to surpass three billion streams, and also broke the record for the fastest song to do so.[\[134\]](#cite_note-135) On January 1, 2023, "Blinding Lights" overtook [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran")'s "[Shape of You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shape_of_You "Shape of You")" to become the [most streamed song of all time on the platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records "List of Spotify streaming records"), with over 3.332 billion streams at the time.[\[135\]](#cite_note-136) On January 12, 2024, it became the first song to pass the 4 billion stream mark on Spotify.[\[136\]](#cite_note-137)

The music video for "Blinding Lights" was directed by Anton Tammi, assisted by Kenneth Taylor, and filmed in [Fremont Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fremont_Street "Fremont Street"), [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas") and [Downtown Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Los_Angeles "Downtown Los Angeles"), during a four-day shooting that took place until 6 AM every day.[\[137\]](#cite_note-138)[\[138\]](#cite_note-VarietyBTS-139)[\[139\]](#cite_note-youtube-140) It was produced by Sarah Parker and executive produced by Saskia Whinney for Somesuch, with production design by Adam William Wilson. Olliver Millar served as the director of photography, assisted by Devin "Daddy" Karringten on the second unit, Niels Lindelien on the steadicam operation, Nizzar Najm on the [gaffer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaffer_\(filmmaking\) "Gaffer (filmmaking)") and Marlow Nunez on the [key grip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_grip "Key grip").[\[139\]](#cite_note-youtube-140) The video was edited by Janne Vartia and Tim Montana, and included [VFX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_effects "Visual effects") by Mathematic, post production surpervision by Alec Ernest, color by Nicke Jacobsson, sound design by Akseli Soini, title design by Aleksi Tammi and 3D effects by Oscar Böckerman.[\[139\]](#cite_note-youtube-140)

The roads were not completely shut down while filming for the street scenes so cars and pedestrians passing are seen in the video while the Weeknd dances in the street. Production was held up temporarily when somebody was arrested in the tunnel.[\[138\]](#cite_note-VarietyBTS-139) The shooting required at least three vehicles driving through the nighttime streets. The [Mercedes-AMG GT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-AMG_GT "Mercedes-AMG GT") roadster was a specially equipped towed vehicle that allowed the Weeknd to act and lip-sync inside the moving convertible without needing to drive, and a chase SUV with a crane camera strapped to the top.[\[140\]](#cite_note-caranddriver-141) Director of photography Oliver Millar said that he loves the music video format and talked about how intense it is to try and create iconic images during high-pressure shoots that don't last very long.[\[140\]](#cite_note-caranddriver-141) He said that since the Weeknd's previous videos had a dark and gritty vibe, he used generators powering banks of LED lights and a Sony Venice full-frame digital motion picture camera system to try to re-create the look, ending up with the video's vintage, 1980s style.[\[138\]](#cite_note-VarietyBTS-139)

### Release and synopsis

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Release and synopsis")\]

On December 2, 2019, a commercial video containing footage from the Weeknd and [Mercedes-Benz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz "Mercedes-Benz") commercial, and the song's audio video, was released.[\[141\]](#cite_note-142) The lyric video for "Blinding Lights" was released on December 6, 2019.[\[142\]](#cite_note-143) Its official music video was released on January 21, 2020.[\[143\]](#cite_note-144) A behind-the-scenes music video for the song was released on February 28, 2020.[\[138\]](#cite_note-VarietyBTS-139) On May 5, 2020, a music video for the [Chromatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatics_\(band\) "Chromatics (band)") remix of the song was released.[\[144\]](#cite_note-145)

The video follows the _After Hours_ videos sequence, starting where the "[Heartless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartless_\(The_Weeknd_song\) "Heartless (The Weeknd song)")" premise ended, and presents the Weeknd as a lonely and psychotic guy walking and driving with no destination around the streets in Las Vegas, and a passing resemblance to jazz musician [Herbie Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbie_Hancock "Herbie Hancock"), circa 1978's _[Sunlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunlight_\(Herbie_Hancock_album\) "Sunlight (Herbie Hancock album)")_.[\[145\]](#cite_note-rsvideo-146) The singer sports the same garb as the previous video, adopted for the album promotion, with a red suit, specific hairstyle, mustache and sunglasses.[\[145\]](#cite_note-rsvideo-146) The visual opens with the Weeknd laughing as blood drips down his face, then jumps back in time to show the mayhem that led to his gruesome end — the pop star speeding around a deserted city, dancing gleefully in the streets.[\[145\]](#cite_note-rsvideo-146) The visual follows the events of the music video for "Heartless" and sees the Weeknd go on a hallucinated joyride after waking from a trance. It concludes with the Weeknd having flashbacks to a club he attended earlier in the night, where he was serenaded by a mysterious woman, played by Japanese actress Miki Hamano and beat up by a duo of bouncers, uncredited, who had forced him to go on the run.[\[146\]](#cite_note-147) The video depicts the singer amid a story inspired by the films _[Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear_and_Loathing_in_Las_Vegas_\(film\) "Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas (film)")_, _[Joker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joker_\(2019_film\) "Joker (2019 film)")_, and _[Casino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casino_\(1995_film\) "Casino (1995 film)")_.[\[147\]](#cite_note-148)

Chase Ichiki from _[Revolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolt_\(TV_network\) "Revolt (TV network)")_ spoke highly of the music video, sharing that "the Weeknd crafts a world fans have eagerly waited for. Donning his staple red suit, he showcases his acting abilities in his latest video. Beginning with him hysterically laughing in a borderline psychotic way, then we see the Weeknd dance the pain away while wandering the city".[\[148\]](#cite_note-149) Michael Cube from _[Nylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nylon_\(magazine\) "Nylon (magazine)")_ magazine wrote that "the video for "Blinding Lights" is appropriately cryptic for the famously elusive artist", and praised the presentation's alluring mystique.[\[149\]](#cite_note-150) _HITC_ columnist Christopher Weston assessed the film as "a burst of neon perfectly complimenting the gorgeous electronic sound. The 'Blinding Lights' visual accompaniment is one of the most stylish videos we've seen, packed with color, fast cars, nocturnal cityscapes and luxurious locations."[\[150\]](#cite_note-151) _[Insider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insider_Inc. "Insider Inc.")_ editor Callie Ahlgrim praised the visual, "'Blinding Lights' embodies everything that's made the Weeknd's newest era so successful. The video maintains his mysterious, slightly menacing [aura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_\(paranormal\) "Aura (paranormal)") — yet manages to create a cinematic, retro, exhilarating experience that's unlike anything he's done before".[\[151\]](#cite_note-152) Bianca Gracie from _[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_\(magazine\) "New York (magazine)")_ named the music video one of the best of 2020: "It's a wild mix of _[Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear_and_Loathing_in_Las_Vegas_\(film\) "Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas (film)")_, [_Casino_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casino_\(1995_film\) "Casino (1995 film)"), and [_Joker_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joker_\(2019_film\) "Joker (2019 film)") that only Abel could pull off".[\[152\]](#cite_note-153) _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")_ editor Gary Dinges named the visual one of the best of 2020.[\[153\]](#cite_note-154) The clip was nominated for six [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards"), and won two including [Best R&B Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_R&B_Video "MTV Video Music Award for Best R&B Video") & [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year").[\[154\]](#cite_note-155) The visual was nominated for four [UK Music Video Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Music_Video_Awards "UK Music Video Awards"), and won Best Pop Video – International.[\[69\]](#cite_note-OfficialVideo-69)

The Weeknd performed "Blinding Lights" for the first time on December 6, 2019, during _[The Late Show with Stephen Colbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Late_Show_with_Stephen_Colbert "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert")_, a day after he performed "Heartless" on the same show.[\[155\]](#cite_note-156) He brought a neon-lit cube with mirrored walls to the stage to sing through his brand new single. Filmed in [black and white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_and_white_film "Black and white film") and from different perspectives on the stage, the Weeknd made the most of his mirror-cube before stepping outside of it to face the crowd.[\[156\]](#cite_note-157) They sang the chorus of the track back to him, and some members of the audience raised mirrors of their own to flash The Weeknd's glow back on him.[\[157\]](#cite_note-158)

The song was performed on January 22, 2020, at _[Jimmy Kimmel Live!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Kimmel_Live! "Jimmy Kimmel Live!")_.[\[158\]](#cite_note-15
