# Blinding Lights

ch 28, 2020, the song rose two places to reach number two.[\[83\]](#cite_note-84) The song reached number one on [R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs "R&B/Hip-Hop Songs") on April 4, 2020, leading for 11 non-consecutive weeks.[\[84\]](#cite_note-Trust-85) The song also reached number one on [R&B Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R&B_Songs "R&B Songs") chart on March 7, 2020, where it became his seventh number one on the chart, making him the artist with the most number ones on the chart's history and also attaining a record-breaking reign of 48 weeks.[\[85\]](#cite_note-86) On March 30, 2020, the song rose to number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, dethroning [Roddy Ricch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roddy_Ricch "Roddy Ricch")'s "[The Box](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Box_\(Roddy_Ricch_song\) "The Box (Roddy Ricch song)")" on the issue dated April 4, 2020.[\[86\]](#cite_note-BH100_Peak-87) The single kept at its peak position the following week, becoming the Weeknd's third multi-week leader after "[The Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hills_\(song\) "The Hills (song)")", which topped the chart five years earlier.[\[87\]](#cite_note-88) "Blinding Lights" spent four weeks atop the Hot 100 and finished 2020 as the [year's top _Billboard_ Hot 100 song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2020 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2020").[\[88\]](#cite_note-BBNo1OfYear-89) The following year, it ranked at number three on the year-end chart, becoming the first single to finish in the top three on two occasions.[\[89\]](#cite_note-90)

"Blinding Lights" spent 57 weeks in the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and 43 weeks in the top five, breaking the record for the most time logged in the region over the chart's 62-year history.[\[90\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-91)[\[91\]](#cite_note-BillboardUSCert-92) On the [Digital Song Sales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Songs "Digital Songs") chart, the song peaked at number one for the week of March 23, 2020, and became the Weeknd's fifth Digital Songs number one. The single reached a peak of number one on the [Streaming Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_Songs "Streaming Songs") chart on March 30, becoming his first topper on the listing since "The Hills" led five years earlier.[\[92\]](#cite_note-93) On April 13, the song reached number one on [Pop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Songs "Pop Songs") chart, where it led for 6 non-consecutive weeks, as it slid to number two on the Hot 100.[\[93\]](#cite_note-94) It later rose back up to number one for the two following weeks.[\[94\]](#cite_note-95)[\[95\]](#cite_note-BB4thweek-96)[\[96\]](#cite_note-97) On May 18, the song became his first number one on the [Adult Pop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Pop_Songs "Adult Pop Songs") chart, leading for 20 non-consecutive weeks.[\[97\]](#cite_note-98) On November 7, "Blinding Lights" became his first number one on the [Adult Contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_\(chart\) "Adult Contemporary (chart)") chart, where it led for 35 non-consecutive weeks.[\[98\]](#cite_note-99)[\[99\]](#cite_note-100) "Blinding Lights" topped [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") for a record-breaking 26 weeks, passing [Goo Goo Dolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goo_Goo_Dolls "Goo Goo Dolls")' "[Iris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_\(song\) "Iris (song)")", which held the record as the longest-running chart-topper for almost 22 years.[\[100\]](#cite_note-101) [\[101\]](#cite_note-102) "Blinding Lights" fell out of the Hot 100 for the week dated January 2, 2021, but it re-entered at number 3 the next week, breaking the three-way tie for the highest song to re-enter the Hot 100.[\[102\]](#cite_note-103)[\[103\]](#cite_note-104) Meanwhile, "Blinding Lights" tied for the most time totaled in the Hot 100's top three, 21 weeks, equaling the sums of The [Chainsmokers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chainsmokers "Chainsmokers")' "[Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Closer (The Chainsmokers song)")" and [Mark Ronson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Ronson "Mark Ronson")'s "[Uptown Funk!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uptown_Funk "Uptown Funk")".[\[90\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-91)

For a short time during 2022, "Blinding Lights" was the longest running single in the history of the Hot 100 chart with a total of 90 weeks, surpassing [Imagine Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imagine_Dragons "Imagine Dragons")' "[Radioactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Radioactive (Imagine Dragons song)")", which spent 87 weeks.[\[80\]](#cite_note-cbc082021-81)[\[104\]](#cite_note-105) In the process, the song also attained the longest chart run of any Hot 100 chart-topper in _Billboard_ history, surpassing the 68-week run by [LMFAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMFAO "LMFAO")'s "[Party Rock Anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Rock_Anthem "Party Rock Anthem")" (2011–12).[\[105\]](#cite_note-106) On November 23, 2021, the song surpassed "[The Twist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twist_\(song\) "The Twist (song)")" (1960) as the [number-one song of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Top_10_songs_of_all_time_\(1958–2021\) "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") in _Billboard_ Hot 100 history.[\[106\]](#cite_note-BBNo1AllTime-107) On April 5, 2022, "Blinding Lights" was awarded a [Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") certification from the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) for selling ten million units in the United States.[\[91\]](#cite_note-BillboardUSCert-92)

"Blinding Lights" also became producer Max Martin's 23rd Hot 100 number one single as a writer, 21st as producer, and his first in both credits since [Justin Timberlake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Timberlake "Justin Timberlake")'s "[Can't Stop the Feeling!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Stop_the_Feeling! "Can't Stop the Feeling!")" (2016). Martin has the third-most as writer, behind [Paul McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney") (32) and [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") (26), and the second-most as producer, behind [George Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Martin "George Martin") (23).[\[86\]](#cite_note-BH100_Peak-87) The Weeknd became the first artist to simultaneously lead _Billboard_'s five primary charts on March 30, topping the Hot 100, [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), [Artist 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artist_100 "Artist 100"), Hot 100 Songwriters and Hot 100 Producers.[\[107\]](#cite_note-108)[\[108\]](#cite_note-109) The next week, he topped the Hot 100, Billboard 200 and Artist 100 once more, achieving the feat for a fourth time.[\[109\]](#cite_note-110)

On the [_Rolling Stone_ Top 100 Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone_Top_100 "Rolling Stone Top 100") chart, the song debuted at number two, where it was blocked from the top spot by the Weeknd's own "[Heartless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartless_\(The_Weeknd_song\) "Heartless (The Weeknd song)")". The song also became the Weeknd's second entry on the chart.[\[110\]](#cite_note-111) It later rose to number one on the chart following the release of _After Hours_.[\[111\]](#cite_note-RS6Months-112)

In the singer's native Canada, "Blinding Lights" debuted at number two on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), one place higher than "Heartless". It later managed to reach number one after the release of its parent album on the issue dated April 4, 2020, becoming the Weeknd's fifth number-one single in the country. It spent seven weeks atop the chart, tying "[Starboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(song\) "Starboy (song)")" as his longest-running chart-topper.[\[112\]](#cite_note-113) In May 2021, "Blinding Lights" dropped off the Canadian Hot 100 after 75 weeks on the chart,[\[113\]](#cite_note-114) leaving it one week short of the all-time record set by "[I Gotta Feeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Gotta_Feeling "I Gotta Feeling")" by the [Black Eyed Peas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Eyed_Peas "Black Eyed Peas") in 2010.[\[114\]](#cite_note-115) For the first half of 2020, "Blinding Lights" was the top Canadian song overall, with 484,000 units.[\[115\]](#cite_note-116) It has been certified Diamond by [Music Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Canada "Music Canada") for selling 800,000 units.[\[116\]](#cite_note-117)

### Europe, Oceania and Latin America

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Europe, Oceania and Latin America")\]

In the United Kingdom,"Blinding Lights" debuted at number 12 on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") on December 6, 2019 – for the week ending date December 12, 2019. It eventually peaked at the top of the chart in February 2020, becoming the Weeknd's first number-one single in Britain.[\[117\]](#cite_note-118) After two weeks at number one, it dropped a place number two. However it rebounded to number one the week after, and remained there for three consecutive weeks. The week after it fell a place to number two and also stayed at the runner-up spot for another week. The following week, it once again rebounded to number one, and stayed there for another three consecutive weeks. Overall, the single spent eight non-consecutive weeks atop the singles chart.[\[118\]](#cite_note-OfficialScores-119)[\[119\]](#cite_note-120) It dropped to number two on April 24, 2020 – for the week ending April 30, 2020 – after the Weeknd used [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") to ask people to support its close rival, a charity single, "[You'll Never Walk Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You'll_Never_Walk_Alone#Michael_Ball_&_Captain_Tom_Moore_version "You'll Never Walk Alone")", by [Michael Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Ball "Michael Ball") and [Captain Sir Tom Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_Tom_Moore "Captain Tom Moore"), and make it number one for Moore's 100th birthday.[\[120\]](#cite_note-Jones-121)[\[121\]](#cite_note-122) As a result, "Blinding Lights" dropped a place to number two and remained at number two the following week, behind another charity single, "[Times Like These](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times_Like_These_\(Foo_Fighters_song\)#Live_Lounge_Allstars_charity_single "Times Like These (Foo Fighters song)")".[\[122\]](#cite_note-OC-123)[\[123\]](#cite_note-OC2-124) According to the [Official Charts Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Charts_Company "Official Charts Company"), "Blinding Lights" became Britain's biggest-selling song of 2020 with 2.2 million combined sales, including 250 million streams and 195,000 downloads.[\[124\]](#cite_note-UKbiggest-125) "Blinding Lights" has been certified 6× Platinum by the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") for selling 3,600,000 units.[\[125\]](#cite_note-126)

Elsewhere in Europe, the song topped the charts in Austria, Belgium, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, the Republic of Ireland, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Sweden, and Switzerland. It also peaked within the top ten of the charts in Belarus, Hungary, Malta, North Macedonia, Russia, Romania, Spain, and Ukraine.

In Australia, it topped the [ARIA Charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts") for eleven non-consecutive weeks. It is the sixth longest-running number-one of all-time in the country, tied with songs such as [Spice Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spice_Girls "Spice Girls")'s "[Wannabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wannabe "Wannabe")", [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)")'s "[God's Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God's_Plan_\(song\) "God's Plan (song)")" and [Bryan Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Adams "Bryan Adams")' "[(Everything I Do) I Do It for You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/\(Everything_I_Do\)_I_Do_It_for_You "(Everything I Do) I Do It for You")", as well the fifth longest by a foreign act.[\[126\]](#cite_note-AriaReturns-127) "Blinding Lights" has been certified 13× Platinum by the [Australian Recording Industry Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Recording_Industry_Association "Australian Recording Industry Association") for selling 910,000 units.[\[127\]](#cite_note-128)

In New Zealand, the song topped the [New Zealand Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand_Singles_Chart "New Zealand Singles Chart") for four non-consecutive weeks.

In Latin America, "Blinding Lights" topped the charts in Bolivia and Mexico. It also reached the top 10 in Chile, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Honduras, Panama, Puerto Rico and Uruguay, as well as the top 20 in Argentina, Nicaragua, Paraguay and Peru. It also charted in Brazil and Colombia, peaking at numbers 51 and 66 respectively.

"Blinding Lights" was the [best-selling global single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles "List of best-selling singles") of 2020, earning 2.72 billion subscription stream equivalents globally. For this feat, it was awarded the IFPI Global Digital Single Award by the [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry") (IFPI).[\[128\]](#cite_note-IFPI-129) It was also the seventh best-selling global single of 2021 with 1.61 billion subscription stream equivalents globally[\[129\]](#cite_note-IFPI2-130) and the fourteenth best-selling global single of 2022 with 1.01 billion subscription stream equivalents globally.[\[130\]](#cite_note-IFPI3-131)

"Blinding Lights" has also broken numerous records on streaming platform [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"). It was the most-streamed song of 2020 on the platform with nearly 1.6 billion streams.[\[131\]](#cite_note-132) On February 24, 2021, it became the first song by a Canadian artist and only the fourth song in history to pass two billion plays on the platform;[\[132\]](#cite_note-133) it also broke the record for the fastest song to do so, in under 15 months.[\[133\]](#cite_note-134) On June 15, 2022, it became the first song by a Canadian artist and only the second song in history to surpass three billion streams, and also broke the record for the fastest song to do so.[\[134\]](#cite_note-135) On January 1, 2023, "Blinding Lights" overtook [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran")'s "[Shape of You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shape_of_You "Shape of You")" to become the [most streamed song of all time on the platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records "List of Spotify streaming records"), with over 3.332 billion streams at the time.[\[135\]](#cite_note-136) On January 12, 2024, it became the first song to pass the 4 billion stream mark on Spotify.[\[136\]](#cite_note-137)

The music video for "Blinding Lights" was directed by Anton Tammi, assisted by Kenneth Taylor, and filmed in [Fremont Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fremont_Street "Fremont Street"), [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas") and [Downtown Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Los_Angeles "Downtown Los Angeles"), during a four-day shooting that took place until 6 AM every day.[\[137\]](#cite_note-138)[\[138\]](#cite_note-VarietyBTS-139)[\[139\]](#cite_note-youtube-140) It was produced by Sarah Parker and executive produced by Saskia Whinney for Somesuch, with production design by Adam William Wilson. Olliver Millar served as the director of photography, assisted by Devin "Daddy" Karringten on the second unit, Niels Lindelien on the steadicam operation, Nizzar Najm on the [gaffer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaffer_\(filmmaking\) "Gaffer (filmmaking)") and Marlow Nunez on the [key grip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_grip "Key grip").[\[139\]](#cite_note-youtube-140) The video was edited by Janne Vartia and Tim Montana, and included [VFX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_effects "Visual effects") by Mathematic, post production surpervision by Alec Ernest, color by Nicke Jacobsson, sound design by Akseli Soini, title design by Aleksi Tammi and 3D effects by Oscar Böckerman.[\[139\]](#cite_note-youtube-140)

The roads were not completely shut down while filming for the street scenes so cars and pedestrians passing are seen in the video while the Weeknd dances in the street. Production was held up temporarily when somebody was arrested in the tunnel.[\[138\]](#cite_note-VarietyBTS-139) The shooting required at least three vehicles driving through the nighttime streets. The [Mercedes-AMG GT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-AMG_GT "Mercedes-AMG GT") roadster was a specially equipped towed vehicle that allowed the Weeknd to act and lip-sync inside the moving convertible without needing to drive, and a chase SUV with a crane camera strapped to the top.[\[140\]](#cite_note-caranddriver-141) Director of photography Oliver Millar said that he loves the music video format and talked about how intense it is to try and create iconic images during high-pressure shoots that don't last very long.[\[140\]](#cite_note-caranddriver-141) He said that since the Weeknd's previous videos had a dark and gritty vibe, he used generators powering banks of LED lights and a Sony Venice full-frame digital motion picture camera system to try to re-create the look, ending up with the video's vintage, 1980s style.[\[138\]](#cite_note-VarietyBTS-139)

### Release and synopsis

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Blinding_Lights&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Release and synopsis")\]

On December 2, 2019, a commercial video containing footage from the Weeknd and [Mercedes-Benz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz "Mercedes-Benz") commercial, and the song's audio video, was released.[\[141\]](#cite_note-142) The lyric video for "Blinding Lights" was released on December 6, 2019.[\[142\]](#cite_note-143) Its official music video was released on January 21, 2020.[\[143\]](#cite_note-144) A behind-the-scenes music video for the song was released on February 28, 2020.[\[138\]](#cite_note-VarietyBTS-139) On May 5, 2020, a music video for the [Chromatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatics_\(band\) "Chromatics (band)") remix of the song was released.[\[144\]](#cite_note-145)

The video follows the _After Hours_ videos sequence, starting where the "[Heartless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartless_\(The_Weeknd_song\) "Heartless (The Weeknd song)")" premise ended, and presents the Weeknd as a lonely and psychotic guy walking and driving with no destination around the streets in Las Vegas, and a passing resemblance to jazz musician [Herbie Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbie_Hancock "Herbie Hancock"), circa 1978's _[Sunlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunlight_\(Herbie_Hancock_album\) "Sunlight (Herbie Hancock album)")_.[\[145\]](#cite_note-rsvideo-146) The singer sports the same garb as the previous video, adopted for the album promotion, with a red suit, specific hairstyle, mustache and sunglasses.[\[145\]](#cite_note-rsvideo-146) The visual opens with the Weeknd laughing as blood drips down his face, then jumps back in time to show the mayhem that led to his gruesome end — the pop star speeding around a deserted city, dancing gleefully in the streets.[\[145\]](#cite_note-rsvideo-146) The visual follows the events of the music video for "Heartless" and sees the Weeknd go on a hallucinated joyride after waking from a trance. It concludes with the Weeknd having flashbacks to a club he attended earlier in the night, where he was serenaded by a mysterious woman, played by Japanese actress Miki Hamano and beat up by a duo of bouncers, uncredited, who had forced him to go on the run.[\[146\]](#cite_note-147) The video depicts the singer amid a story inspired by the films _[Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear_and_Loathing_in_Las_Vegas_\(film\) "Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas (film)")_, _[Joker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joker_\(2019_film\) "Joker (2019 film)")_, and _[Casino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casino_\(1995_film\) "Casino (1995 film)")_.[\[147\]](#cite_note-148)

Chase Ichiki from _[Revolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolt_\(TV_network\) "Revolt (TV network)")_ spoke highly of the music video, sharing that "the Weeknd crafts a world fans have eagerly waited for. Donning his staple red suit, he showcases his acting abilities in his latest video. Beginning with him hysterically laughing in a borderline psychotic way, then we see the Weeknd dance the pain away while wandering the city".[\[148\]](#cite_note-149) Michael Cube from _[Nylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nylon_\(magazine\) "Nylon (magazine)")_ magazine wrote that "the video for "Blinding Lights" is appropriately cryptic for the famously elusive artist", and praised the presentation's alluring mystique.[\[149\]](#cite_note-150) _HITC_ columnist Christopher Weston assessed the film as "a burst of neon perfectly complimenting the gorgeous electronic sound. The 'Blinding Lights' visual accompaniment is one of the most stylish videos we've seen, packed with color, fast cars, nocturnal cityscapes and luxurious locations."[\[150\]](#cite_note-151) _[Insider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insider_Inc. "Insider Inc.")_ editor Callie Ahlgrim praised the visual, "'Blinding Lights' embodies everything that's made the Weeknd's newest era so successful. The video maintains his mysterious, slightly menacing [aura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aura_\(paranormal\) "Aura (paranormal)") — yet manages to create a cinematic, retro, exhilarating experience that's unlike anything he's done before".[\[151\]](#cite_note-152) Bianca Gracie from _[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_\(magazine\) "New York (magazine)")_ named the music video one of the best of 2020: "It's a wild mix of _[Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear_and_Loathing_in_Las_Vegas_\(film\) "Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas (film)")_, [_Casino_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casino_\(1995_film\) "Casino (1995 film)"), and [_Joker_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joker_\(2019_film\) "Joker (2019 film)") that only Abel could pull off".[\[152\]](#cite_note-153) _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")_ editor Gary Dinges named the visual one of the best of 2020.[\[153\]](#cite_note-154) The clip was nominated for six [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards"), and won two including [Best R&B Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_R&B_Video "MTV Video Music Award for Best R&B Video") & [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year").[\[154\]](#cite_note-155) The visual was nominated for four [UK Music Video Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Music_Video_Awards "UK Music Video Awards"), and won Best Pop Video – International.[\[69\]](#cite_note-OfficialVideo-69)

The Weeknd performed "Blinding Lights" for the first time on December 6, 2019, during _[The Late Show with Stephen Colbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Late_Show_with_Stephen_Colbert "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert")_, a day after he performed "Heartless" on the same show.[\[155\]](#cite_note-156) He brought a neon-lit cube with mirrored walls to the stage to sing through his brand new single. Filmed in [black and white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_and_white_film "Black and white film") and from different perspectives on the stage, the Weeknd made the most of his mirror-cube before stepping outside of it to face the crowd.[\[156\]](#cite_note-157) They sang the chorus of the track back to him, and some members of the audience raised mirrors of their own to flash The Weeknd's glow back on him.[\[157\]](#cite_note-158)

# Max Martin

 "Just like Fire")" (2016), for various Pink-related projects. For her seventh studio album, _[Beautiful Trauma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beautiful_Trauma "Beautiful Trauma")_ (2017), he co-wrote "[Revenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revenge_\(Pink_song\) "Revenge (Pink song)")", "[Whatever You Want](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whatever_You_Want_\(Pink_song\) "Whatever You Want (Pink song)")", "For Now", and "Secrets". In 2019, for her eighth studio album, _[Hurts 2B Human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurts_2B_Human "Hurts 2B Human")_ (2019), he co-wrote "(Hey Why) Miss You Sometime". In 2023, he co-wrote and co-produced lead single "[Never Gonna Not Dance Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Gonna_Not_Dance_Again "Never Gonna Not Dance Again")" from her eighth studio album _[Trustfall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trustfall "Trustfall")_.

In 2010, Martin co-wrote and co-produced [Usher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usher_\(singer\) "Usher (singer)")'s song "[DJ Got Us Fallin' in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Got_Us_Fallin'_in_Love "DJ Got Us Fallin' in Love")" that went number-one on the US [Rhythmic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_\(chart\) "Rhythmic (chart)") charts and top-ten on the main Hot 100.[\[40\]](#cite_note-40) In 2011, Usher and Martin co-wrote single "[Fast Car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Car_\(Taio_Cruz_song\) "Fast Car (Taio Cruz song)")" from the 2012 repackage of [Taio Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taio_Cruz "Taio Cruz")'s third album _[TY.O](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TY.O "TY.O")_. Working together again, Martin co-wrote and co-produced on Usher's seventh studio album _[Looking 4 Myself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Looking_4_Myself "Looking 4 Myself")_ in 2012 making the [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop") song "[Scream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scream_\(Usher_song\) "Scream (Usher song)")" that went number-one on the US [Dance Club Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_Club_Songs "Dance Club Songs") chart and number nine on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart. It was certified platinum by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA).[\[41\]](#cite_note-41)

Martin worked with [Avril Lavigne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avril_Lavigne "Avril Lavigne") on two songs, "Alone" and "I Will Be", which were released on some deluxe editions of Lavigne's third studio album _[The Best Damn Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Best_Damn_Thing "The Best Damn Thing")_ (2007). In 2010, "[Dancing Crazy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing_Crazy "Dancing Crazy")", a song they co-wrote and Martin co-produced in the _[Goodbye Lullaby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye_Lullaby "Goodbye Lullaby")_ sessions, was released by [Miranda Cosgrove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Cosgrove "Miranda Cosgrove") and charted at #100 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart. Martin would later work on four additional songs for Lavigne's fourth studio album _Goodbye Lullaby_ (2011): the three singles "[What the Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_the_Hell "What the Hell")" (2011), "[Smile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smile_\(Avril_Lavigne_song\) "Smile (Avril Lavigne song)")" (2011), and "[Wish You Were Here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wish_You_Were_Here_\(Avril_Lavigne_song\) "Wish You Were Here (Avril Lavigne song)")" (2011), and album track "I Love You".

Max Martin first worked with [Jessie J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessie_J "Jessie J") on her international hit "[Domino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domino_\(Jessie_J_song\) "Domino (Jessie J song)")",[\[42\]](#cite_note-42) which achieved top ten success in countries including Canada, The United States, and Australia. Following the success of "Domino", Martin co-produced "[Bang Bang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bang_Bang_\(Jessie_J,_Ariana_Grande_and_Nicki_Minaj_song\) "Bang Bang (Jessie J, Ariana Grande and Nicki Minaj song)")" (2014) for Jessie J, [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande") and [Nicki Minaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj").

Max Martin worked with [Katy Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Perry "Katy Perry") on her second album _[One of the Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_of_the_Boys_\(Katy_Perry_album\) "One of the Boys (Katy Perry album)")_ (2008), including the number-one single "[I Kissed a Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Kissed_a_Girl "I Kissed a Girl")", and top 5 hit single "[Hot n Cold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_n_Cold "Hot n Cold")". He also worked on her follow-up album _[Teenage Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage_Dream_\(Katy_Perry_album\) "Teenage Dream (Katy Perry album)")_ (2010), including the _Billboard_ Hot 100 numbers-one hit singles "[California Gurls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Gurls "California Gurls")" (2010), "[Teenage Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage_Dream_\(Katy_Perry_song\) "Teenage Dream (Katy Perry song)")" (2010), "[E.T.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.T._\(song\) "E.T. (song)")" (2011),"[Last Friday Night (T.G.I.F.)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Friday_Night_\(T.G.I.F.\) "Last Friday Night (T.G.I.F.)")" (2011) and the top ten hit "[The One That Got Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_One_That_Got_Away_\(Katy_Perry_song\) "The One That Got Away (Katy Perry song)")" (2011). Martin also co-wrote the songs "[Part of Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Part_of_Me_\(Katy_Perry_song\) "Part of Me (Katy Perry song)")" (2012) and "[Wide Awake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_Awake_\(Katy_Perry_song\) "Wide Awake (Katy Perry song)")" (2012), the former of which topped the _Billboard_ Hot 100.

For her fourth album _[Prism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prism_\(Katy_Perry_album\) "Prism (Katy Perry album)")_ (2013), he co-wrote and produced ten of its songs, including the No. 1 singles "[Roar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roar_\(song\) "Roar (song)")" (2013) and "[Dark Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_Horse_\(Katy_Perry_song\) "Dark Horse (Katy Perry song)")" (2013). In 2016, Martin and Perry collaborated on standalone single "[Rise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rise_\(Katy_Perry_song\) "Rise (Katy Perry song)")" for the NBC Coverage of the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics"), reaching number 11 on the Billboard Hot 100.

On her fifth album _[Witness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witness_\(Katy_Perry_album\) "Witness (Katy Perry album)")_ (2017), Martin co-wrote numerous songs, including the lead single "[Chained to the Rhythm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chained_to_the_Rhythm "Chained to the Rhythm")" which peaked at number 4 on the Hot 100, as well as the title track. In 2024, Martin would reunite with Perry, co-writing "Gorgeous" from her seventh studio album _[143](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/143_\(Katy_Perry_album\) "143 (Katy Perry album)")_.

Confirmed by RCA Executives on 18 December 2011, Martin worked on [Christina Aguilera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Aguilera "Christina Aguilera")'s seventh studio album _[Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_\(Christina_Aguilera_album\) "Lotus (Christina Aguilera album)")_ (2012) and was the producer of her lead single, "[Your Body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Your_Body_\(Christina_Aguilera_song\) "Your Body (Christina Aguilera song)")" (2012), as well as another song titled "[Let There Be Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let_There_Be_Love_\(Christina_Aguilera_song\) "Let There Be Love (Christina Aguilera song)")". Both songs reached the top of the _Billboard_ dance/club chart.

Martin has collaborated with [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") on four of her albums. Their first collaboration was the _Billboard_ Hot 100 number-one hit "[We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Never_Ever_Getting_Back_Together "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together")" (2012) for her album _[Red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_\(Taylor_Swift_album\) "Red (Taylor Swift album)")_ (2012). Martin also co-wrote and co-produced two other singles on the album: "[I Knew You Were Trouble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Knew_You_Were_Trouble "I Knew You Were Trouble")" (2012), which peaked at number two on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, and "[22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/22_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "22 (Taylor Swift song)")" (2013). He co-wrote "[Message in a Bottle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Message_in_a_Bottle_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Message in a Bottle (Taylor Swift song)")" for _Red_, but it was not released until 2021, when it was included on _[Red (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_\(Taylor's_Version\) "Red (Taylor's Version)")_ and issued as a single.

Martin also contributed to her follow-up record, _[1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_\(album\) "1989 (album)")_ (2014). He co-wrote and co-produced ten songs, including the singles "[Shake It Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shake_It_Off "Shake It Off")", "[Blank Space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blank_Space "Blank Space")", "[Bad Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Blood_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Bad Blood (Taylor Swift song)")", "[Wildest Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildest_Dreams_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Wildest Dreams (Taylor Swift song)")", "[Style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Style_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Style (Taylor Swift song)")", and "[New Romantics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Romantics_\(song\) "New Romantics (song)")".[\[43\]](#cite_note-43) The former three songs reached number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[\[44\]](#cite_note-44)

Martin later worked with Swift on _[Reputation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reputation_\(album\) "Reputation (album)")_ (2017), co-writing and co-producing eight songs, including the singles "[...Ready for It?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/...Ready_for_It%3F "...Ready for It?")", "[End Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_Game_\(song\) "End Game (song)")", and "[Delicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delicate_\(Taylor_Swift_song\) "Delicate (Taylor Swift song)")".

In August 2025, Swift announced her twelfth album _[The Life of a Showgirl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Life_of_a_Showgirl "The Life of a Showgirl")_, with Martin co-producing alongside Swift and Shellback.[\[45\]](#cite_note-45)

Martin first worked with [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande") on her second studio album _[My Everything](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Everything_\(Ariana_Grande_album\) "My Everything (Ariana Grande album)")_ (2014). Martin produced the first single, "[Problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problem_\(Ariana_Grande_song\) "Problem (Ariana Grande song)")", which peaked at No. 2 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 as well as No. 1 in the UK, later becoming one of the [list of best-selling singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles "List of best-selling singles"). Other songs from the album Martin produced include "[Break Free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Break_Free_\(song\) "Break Free (song)")" (peaking at No. 4 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100) and "[Bang Bang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bang_Bang_\(Jessie_J,_Ariana_Grande_and_Nicki_Minaj_song\) "Bang Bang (Jessie J, Ariana Grande and Nicki Minaj song)")" (peaking at No. 3 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and No. 1 in the UK).

Martin contributed heavily to her third studio album, _[Dangerous Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerous_Woman "Dangerous Woman")_ (2016), most notably the singles "[Dangerous Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerous_Woman_\(Ariana_Grande_song\) "Dangerous Woman (Ariana Grande song)")", "[Into You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Into_You_\(Ariana_Grande_song\) "Into You (Ariana Grande song)")", and "[Side to Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Side_to_Side "Side to Side")", all of which peaked within the top twenty on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.

Martin also contributed to her follow-up records _[Sweetener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweetener_\(album\) "Sweetener (album)")_ (2018) and _[Thank U, Next](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank_U,_Next "Thank U, Next")_ (2019), co-writing the singles "[No Tears Left to Cry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Tears_Left_to_Cry "No Tears Left to Cry")", "[God Is a Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_Is_a_Woman "God Is a Woman")", and "[Break Up with Your Girlfriend, I'm Bored](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Break_Up_with_Your_Girlfriend,_I'm_Bored "Break Up with Your Girlfriend, I'm Bored")", among other songs.

Grande released her lead single "[Yes, And?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yes,_And%3F "Yes, And?")" from her seventh studio album _[Eternal Sunshine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal_Sunshine_\(album\) "Eternal Sunshine (album)")_ on 12 January 2024. She wrote and produced the song with Martin and Ilya Salmanzadeh. Martin also co-wrote and co-produced 10 other tracks from the album, including "[We Can't Be Friends (Wait for Your Love)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Can't_Be_Friends_\(Wait_for_Your_Love\) "We Can't Be Friends (Wait for Your Love)")". He would later co-write and co-produce all five new songs on her 2025 reissue _[Eternal Sunshine Deluxe: Brighter Days Ahead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal_Sunshine_Deluxe:_Brighter_Days_Ahead "Eternal Sunshine Deluxe: Brighter Days Ahead")_, which all charted on the Billboard Hot 100 chart.

In 2026, it was revealed that Martin had co-written and co-produced Grande's album [Petal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petal_\(album\) "Petal (album)"), including the number one single "[Hate That I Made You Love Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hate_That_I_Made_You_Love_Me "Hate That I Made You Love Me")".

Martin co-wrote and produced three songs from [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd")'s sophomore album, _[Beauty Behind the Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_Behind_the_Madness "Beauty Behind the Madness") (2015)_, namely "[Can't Feel My Face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Feel_My_Face "Can't Feel My Face")"—which peaked at number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100—"[In the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_the_Night_\(The_Weeknd_song\) "In the Night (The Weeknd song)")" and "Shameless". He co-wrote and produced four songs ("[Rockin'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockin'_\(song\) "Rockin' (song)")", "Love To Lay", "[A Lonely Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Lonely_Night "A Lonely Night")", and "Ordinary Life") from the Weeknd's third album, _[Starboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(album\) "Starboy (album)")_ (2016).[\[46\]](#cite_note-46)

He contributed "[Hardest to Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardest_to_Love "Hardest to Love")", "[Scared to Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scared_to_Live "Scared to Live")", "[Blinding Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blinding_Lights "Blinding Lights")", "[In Your Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_Your_Eyes_\(The_Weeknd_song\) "In Your Eyes (The Weeknd song)")", and "[Save Your Tears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_Your_Tears "Save Your Tears")" to the Weeknd's fourth studio album, _[After Hours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_Hours_\(The_Weeknd_album\) "After Hours (The Weeknd album)")_ (2020). The latter album was both a critical and commercial success.

Martin also co-wrote and assisted in the production of "[Take My Breath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take_My_Breath "Take My Breath")", released in August 2021. He also produced or co produced the majority of the songs on the Weeknd's fifth studio album _[Dawn FM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawn_FM "Dawn FM")_ (2022).

Martin appears on The Weeknd's sixth studio album _[Hurry Up Tomorrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurry_Up_Tomorrow "Hurry Up Tomorrow")_ (2025), co-writing and/or producing the songs "[Open Hearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_Hearts_\(song\) "Open Hearts (song)") ", "Give Me Mercy", "Drive", "Society", "Runaway", and discarded lead single "[Dancing in the Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing_in_the_Flames "Dancing in the Flames")".

Martin appeared as a keyboardist on two singles from [Coldplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coldplay "Coldplay")'s eighth studio album _[Everyday Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everyday_Life_\(Coldplay_album\) "Everyday Life (Coldplay album)")_ (2019): "[Orphans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orphans_\(Coldplay_song\) "Orphans (Coldplay song)")" and "[Champion of the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champion_of_the_World_\(song\) "Champion of the World (song)")". In June 2021, Coldplay announced their ninth studio album [_Music of the Spheres_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_the_Spheres_\(Coldplay_album\) "Music of the Spheres (Coldplay album)") (2021), with Martin serving as the album's producer.[\[47\]](#cite_note-47) The album received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, debuting at the top of the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") and becoming the album with most sales in a week in the United Kingdom since [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran")'s _[No.6 Collaborations Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No.6_Collaborations_Project "No.6 Collaborations Project")_ (2019).[\[48\]](#cite_note-48)

_[Music of the Spheres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_the_Spheres_\(Coldplay_album\) "Music of the Spheres (Coldplay album)")_ (2021) included songs such as "[Higher Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_Power_\(Coldplay_song\) "Higher Power (Coldplay song)")", "[Let Somebody Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let_Somebody_Go "Let Somebody Go")", which [Selena Gomez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selena_Gomez "Selena Gomez") appears on, and "[My Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Universe_\(song\) "My Universe (song)")", which [BTS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BTS "BTS") appears on. "My Universe" debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, giving Martin his twenty fifth number one as a writer and twenty third number one as a producer on the chart.[\[49\]](#cite_note-49) With that song, he tied with [George Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Martin "George Martin") for producer with most _Billboard_ Hot 100 number ones. (He would later pass Martin.[\[50\]](#cite_note-50)) He recently co-wrote and co-produced a majority of their 2024 studio album _[Moon Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon_Music "Moon Music")_.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/31/Max_Martin.jpg/250px-Max_Martin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Max_Martin.jpg)

Martin in 2015

Martin co-wrote "[It's My Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_My_Life_\(Bon_Jovi_song\) "It's My Life (Bon Jovi song)")" with fellow [Songwriters Hall of Fame inductees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Songwriters_Hall_of_Fame_inductees "List of Songwriters Hall of Fame inductees") [Jon Bon Jovi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Bon_Jovi "Jon Bon Jovi") and [Richie Sambora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richie_Sambora "Richie Sambora"). It was released on 8 May 2000 as the lead single from [Bon Jovi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bon_Jovi "Bon Jovi")'s seventh studio album, _[Crush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crush_\(Bon_Jovi_album\) "Crush (Bon Jovi album)")_. The song was certified 6× platinum in Australia; 3× platinum in the United States; 2× platinum in New Zealand, Spain, and the United Kingdom; platinum in Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Italy, Sweden, and Switzerland; and gold in Brazil, France, Japan, and the Netherlands.[\[51\]](#cite_note-51)

Fourth runner-up of the eighth season of _[American Idol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Idol_\(season_8\) "American Idol (season 8)")_ [Allison Iraheta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allison_Iraheta "Allison Iraheta") collaborated with Martin on her debut album. Her first single, "[Friday I'll Be Over U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friday_I'll_Be_Over_U "Friday I'll Be Over U")" was written by Martin.[\[52\]](#cite_note-52) On 17 August 2009, _American Idol_ runner-up [Adam Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Lambert "Adam Lambert") announced via [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") that he was in New York City with Martin recording a song for his debut album. It turned out to be the song "[Whataya Want From Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whataya_Want_From_Me "Whataya Want From Me")";[\[53\]](#cite_note-53) that was also written by [P!nk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pink_\(singer\) "Pink (singer)").

Martin also co-wrote "[Into the Nightlife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Into_the_Nightlife "Into the Nightlife")", a popular club track recorded by [Cyndi Lauper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyndi_Lauper "Cyndi Lauper") in 2008 and produced, alongside Zedd, and co-wrote "[Beauty and a Beat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_and_a_Beat "Beauty and a Beat")", on [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s 2012 album _[Believe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believe_\(Justin_Bieber_album\) "Believe (Justin Bieber album)")_.

Martin also produced several albums for [Eurodance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurodance "Eurodance") act [E-type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-Type_\(musician\) "E-Type (musician)").

In 2005, Max Martin wrote the first single-song for [pop-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop-punk "Pop-punk") duo [the Veronicas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Veronicas "The Veronicas"), "[4ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4ever_\(The_Veronicas_song\) "4ever (The Veronicas song)")", with Lukasz "[Dr. Luke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Luke "Dr. Luke")" Gottwald, for their debut studio album _[The Secret Life Of...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Secret_Life_Of..._\(album\) "The Secret Life Of... (album)")_ (2005). Also he wrote "[Everything I'm Not](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everything_I'm_Not "Everything I'm Not")", the second single-song of the Veronicas, the same year, again with Gottwald, [Rami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rami_Yacoub "Rami Yacoub"), [Jessica Origliasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jessica_Origliasso "Jessica Origliasso") and [Lisa Origliasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Origliasso "Lisa Origliasso") for the same album.

In January 2014, Martin produced a two-minute advertisement entitled "Volvo XC70: Made By Sweden",[\[54\]](#cite_note-54) featuring soccer player [Zlatan Ibrahimović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zlatan_Ibrahimović "Zlatan Ibrahimović"). The video of the advertisement received several million views on YouTube.

2008 saw him collaborate with [Daughtry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daughtry_\(band\) "Daughtry (band)") for one of their singles from their 2006 debut album [_Daughtry_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daughtry_\(album\) "Daughtry (album)"): the song "[Feels Like Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feels_Like_Tonight "Feels Like Tonight")" written with [Dr. Luke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Luke "Dr. Luke").

In early 2014, Martin co-wrote the song "Dare (La La La)" for [Shakira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakira "Shakira")'s [self-titled album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakira_\(album\) "Shakira (album)").

In April–May 2014, Martin produced [Jennifer Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lopez "Jennifer Lopez")'s song "[First Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Love_\(Jennifer_Lopez_song\) "First Love (Jennifer Lopez song)")", alongside [Ilya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilya_\(record_producer\) "Ilya (record producer)"), [Shellback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shellback_\(record_producer\) "Shellback (record producer)") and [Savan Kotecha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savan_Kotecha "Savan Kotecha").

Between 2014 and 2015, Martin produced singles "[Ghost Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghost_Town_\(Adam_Lambert_song\) "Ghost Town (Adam Lambert song)")" and "[Another Lonely Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Lonely_Night_\(Adam_Lambert_song\) "Another Lonely Night (Adam Lambert song)")" by [Adam Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Lambert "Adam Lambert"), before executive-producing his third studio album _[The Original High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Original_High "The Original High")_.

In January 2015, he co-wrote and co-produced [Ellie Goulding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellie_Goulding "Ellie Goulding")'s "[Love Me like You Do](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Me_like_You_Do "Love Me like You Do")", which reached number 3 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"),[\[55\]](#cite_note-55) while also producing several songs from her album [_Delirium_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delirium_\(Ellie_Goulding_album\) "Delirium (Ellie Goulding album)") including the hit single "[On My Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_My_Mind_\(Ellie_Goulding_song\) "On My Mind (Ellie Goulding song)")", which was released on 17 September 2015.

In July 2015, Martin produced [Demi Lovato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demi_Lovato "Demi Lovato")'s song "[Cool for the Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cool_for_the_Summer "Cool for the Summer")" which reached number 11 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). He also contributed to "[Confident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confident_\(Demi_Lovato_song\) "Confident (Demi Lovato song)")" and "For You" from their fifth studio album _[Confident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confident_\(album\) "Confident (album)")_.

Martin also worked with [Selena Gomez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selena_Gomez "Selena Gomez") on her second studio album, _[Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revival_\(Selena_Gomez_album\) "Revival (Selena Gomez album)")_, producing its third single "[Hands to Myself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hands_to_Myself "Hands to Myself")", which became her third consecutive top 10 hit from the album.

In November 2015, [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele")'s album _[25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/25_\(Adele_album\) "25 (Adele album)")_ was released and Martin co-wrote and co-produced the record's third single "[Send My Love (To Your New Lover)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Send_My_Love_\(To_Your_New_Lover\) "Send My Love (To Your New Lover)")" with Shellback; it would eventually become a top 10 hit in the US and the UK.

In 2016, he co-wrote the song "[Can't Stop the Feeling!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Stop_the_Feeling! "Can't Stop the Feeling!")" by [Justin Timberlake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Timberlake "Justin Timberlake") which is also the title song for the film _[Trolls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trolls_\(film\) "Trolls (film)")_ with Shellback. The song became Timberlake's fifth and Martin's twenty-second number-one hit in the US.[\[56\]](#cite_note-56) It reached the top spot in 16 other countries. The song gave Timberlake and Martin their first nomination for an [Academy Award for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song").

In 2019, Martin co-produced and co-wrote [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran")'s and [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s hit single "[I Don't Care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don't_Care_\(Ed_Sheeran_and_Justin_Bieber_song\) "I Don't Care (Ed Sheeran and Justin Bieber song)")".[\[57\]](#cite_note-57) Martin also co-wrote [Sam Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Smith "Sam Smith")'s single "[How Do You Sleep?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_You_Sleep%3F_\(Sam_Smith_song\) "How Do You Sleep? (Sam Smith song)")".

In November 2019, Martin co-wrote and co-produced the Weeknd's single "Blinding Lights".[\[58\]](#cite_note-58)[\[59\]](#cite_note-59)[\[60\]](#cite_note-60)

In 2020, Martin co-produced and co-wrote "[Stupid Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stupid_Love_\(Lady_Gaga_song\) "Stupid Love (Lady Gaga song)")", the first single from [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga")'s sixth studio album, _[Chromatica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatica "Chromatica")_. This marks the first time the two have worked together.[\[61\]](#cite_note-61)

In 2021, Martin co-wrote and co-produced "[Can I Get It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can_I_Get_It "Can I Get It")" by Adele from her fourth studio album, _[30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/30_\(album\) "30 (album)")_.

In 2022, Martin co-produced and co-wrote [Måneskin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Måneskin "Måneskin")'s single "[Supermodel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supermodel_\(Måneskin_song\) "Supermodel (Måneskin song)")".[\[62\]](#cite_note-62) He also co-produced and co-wrote [Lizzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lizzo "Lizzo")'s song "2 Be Loved (Am I Ready)", from her fourth studio album, [_Special_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_\(Lizzo_album\) "Special (Lizzo album)").[\[63\]](#cite_note-63)

In 2023, Martin co-wrote and co-produced [Conan Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_Gray "Conan Gray")'s singles "Never Ending Song" and "Killing Me". He also co-wrote and co-produced Ed Sheeran's single "[Eyes Closed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyes_Closed_\(Ed_Sheeran_song\) "Eyes Closed (Ed Sheeran song)")" from his fifth studio album.

When accepting the [Polar Music Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_Music_Prize "Polar Music Prize"), M
