_[The Weeknd](https://www.billboard.com/t/the-weeknd/)‘s “Blinding Lights” is the new No. 1 song on_ Billboard_’s Greatest Songs of All Time Hot 100 Chart. In celebration,_ Billboard _is launching a special [collection of trading cards](https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/the-weeknd-trading-card-nft-collection-1235001566/) which will be followed by the debut of a limited-edition NFT collection._

[Chubby Checker](https://www.billboard.com/artist/chubby-checker/) once described the steps of his 1960 chart-topping hit [“The Twist”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-CCgDvUM4TM&ab_channel=ChubbyCheckerVEVO) as someone swiveling their hips, swinging their arms in the opposite direction and twisting their feet as if they were putting out a cigarette. The song and dance were simple but irresistible: Thanks to separate chart runs in 1960 and again in 1962, “The Twist” was named _Billboard_’s all-time [Hot 100](https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/) No. 1 single in 2008, a designation that factors in total weeks on the chart as well as exact chart positions, with weeks at No. 1 earning the greatest value and weeks at No. 100 earning the least. (Due to changes in chart methodology over the years, eras are weighted differently to account for chart turnover rates during various periods.) To this day, Checker boasts [on his website](https://www.chubbychecker.com/index.asp) that it’s an achievement no one else will claim “until 2065.”

Then came [The Weeknd](https://www.billboard.com/artist/the-weeknd/). In early 2020, the singer born Abel Tesfaye released an ominous music video that saw him doing his own little shuffle, swaying his hips and gingerly tapping his feet to a song, “Blinding Lights,” that had debuted just two months before — and which would soon leave its own mark on pop history. Though Tesfaye, 31, had topped plenty of charts before, the adrenaline-pumping synth-pop track (created with help from legendary songwriter-producer Max Martin) marked the final stage of his evolution from enigmatic breakout of Toronto’s underground R&B scene to genre-busting icon. And with cinematic, high-concept visuals and performances that took him all the way to the Super Bowl halftime show — all starring a mysterious red-jacketed, increasingly bruised and bandaged character Tesfaye played throughout — “Blinding Lights” and the album that accompanied it, _After Hours_, also cemented Tesfaye as not just a radio fixture, but an auteur in his own right.

“I feel like I’ve been making that record for a decade,” Tesfaye says with a sigh today. “Blinding Lights” had a slow burn, reaching the top of the Hot 100 in March 2020, the same week _After Hours_ debuted atop the [Billboard 200](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-200/). But once it took hold, listeners wouldn’t let it go: The four-week No. 1 smash shattered the record for most weeks spent in the top five (43 weeks), top 10 (57), top 40 (86) and on the Hot 100 (90) — enough to dethrone “The Twist” on _Billboard_’s Greatest of All Time Hot 100 chart by the end of its chart run in September.

“From the first time I met Abel, it was clear that he was destined for global stardom,” says Republic Records co-founder/CEO Monte Lipman. “And it’s just one of those cases where the stars aligned. ‘Blinding Lights’ went into the zeitgeist and became one of those songs that just had this emotional impact on so many people around the world.”

* * *

### **“There Was Nothing We Had Heard Like That Before From Abel.”**

_After exorcising some personal demons with the 2018 EP_ My Dear Melancholy_, — a dark, muted throwback to his early work — Tesfaye was ready to play pop star again on his fourth studio album. He convened an all-star crew — including Swedish superproducer Martin, who had helped him score his first Hot 100 No. 1 with “Can’t Feel My Face” — as well as longtime collaborators and co-writers like Jason “DaHeala” Quenneville and Ahmad “Belly” Balshe to channel his love of 1980s pop music and video-game soundtracks into radio-friendly anthems. The material came easily and quickly — he recorded_ After Hours _tracks “Scared To Live” and “Save Your Tears” during the same session at New York’s Jungle City Studios as “Blinding Lights.”_

**Abel “The Weeknd” Tesfaye:** _My Dear Melancholy_, was one of those things I had to just get off my chest, and I didn’t really want anyone’s input. So I was excited to be in the studio again with collaborators I love. You can only imagine how quick those songs came.

**Max Martin, co-producer/writer:** Abel came with the vision of what the song should be, which was a very different tempo and vibe than what is usually done. He took a risk, and that was very impressive to us. We all felt this song was very special even early on in the process.

**Tesfaye:** _GTA: Vice City_ really opened my eyes to a lot of ’80s music, so there was a nostalgia for when I was a kid playing video games and listening to Hall & Oates and Michael Jackson while driving through the city.

![The Weeknd](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/feature-the-weeknd-billboard-2021-bb16-brian-ziff-2-650.jpg?w=650)

Set Design by Walter Barnett at Opus Beauty. Hair by Daronn Carr at Blend LA. Makeup by Christine Nelli at The Wall Group. On-Set Styling by Breaunna Trask. Tom Ford shirt, Saint Laurent pants, Rick Owens jacket and shoes. Photographed by Brian Ziff

**Martin:** My engineer Sam \[Holland\] had brought up equipment to project on the wall a computer-animated car driving through a futuristic city for inspiration. I hadn’t seen something like that before, and Abel came in and loved it.

**Tesfaye:** Me and Max hadn’t worked together since the _Starboy_ album, so we were excited to connect again. And it was the first time I worked with Oscar \[Holter, a close Martin collaborator\], and that was instantly kismet. And Belly and DaHeala are my guys — anything I do, I feel like I have to bounce ideas off them.

**Ahmad “Belly” Balshe, co-writer:** Getting to watch the great Max Martin and Abel create is a dream in itself, and I’m just beyond honored and proud to be a part of something this legendary.

**Monte Lipman, co-founder/CEO, Republic Records:** During a playback of an early version of _After Hours_ in the studio, I was like, “Whoa, what was that?” We actually made him play it a couple more times. There was nothing we had heard like that before from Abel.

**Tesfaye:** I’ve always been tinkering with the \[sounds of the\] ’80s. It was much more subtle before, but I’ve always wanted to completely dive into it. And 10 years in, I think I’ve earned it.

**Wassim “Sal” Slaiby, manager; co-founder/CEO, XO Records:** He’s got that power to take something and make it cool, make it edgy, make it risky, make it kid-friendly.

**La Mar C. Taylor, creative director; co-founder, XO Records:** He knows exactly what he wants. If you’re a true Weeknd fan, then you understand sonically where he was going with his music. He was always headed in this direction. It was always building up to something like this. It was such an ambitious record for Abel at the time. It was either going to be the biggest song in the world — or go over people’s heads.

* * *

Just as he had shed the freeform locs of his “Can’t Feel My Face” days for a sharper look during his_ Starboy _rollout in 2016, the singer sought a new look for_ After Hours_, turning to renowned Hollywood tailor Fresh (who had previously worked on suits for his red-carpet appearances and other events) to transform him into a nameless character inspired by Las Vegas noir. With his signature red blazer, he became central to The Weeknd’s “Blinding Lights” performances and subsequent music videos, which followed the character on a disorienting, violent odyssey through the glitz and grit of Sin City — and inspired countless Reddit threads trying to unpack its meaning._

**Tesfaye:** I toyed with the idea with _Starboy_ and _Beauty Behind the Madness_ — in the videos, I was telling a throughline story. So I feel like _After Hours_ is me executing it at full potential, and me going full Method on it.

![The Weeknd](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/feature-the-weeknd-billboard-2021-bb16-brian-ziff-3-650.jpg?w=650)

Photographed by Brian Ziff

**Fresh, tailor:** He told me he had some ideas for his new album, and he wanted to try this suit concept out. He gave me some movies to watch.

**Tesfaye:** From Jack Nicholson’s character in _Chinatown_ to the film _Possession_ to Tim Robbins in _Jacob’s Ladder_, it’s just all of my favorite psychological thrillers and dramas in one universe.

**Taylor:** There was a nod to Nicolas Cage in _Leaving Las Vegas_, _Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas_, _Casino_ by Martin Scorsese — really iconic Las Vegas cinema. We were just trying to pay respect to those great actors and filmmakers that really created our world for us.

**Slaiby:** When you see the “Heartless” video, he’s building that character for you. It wouldn’t make sense to just build the character where \[“Blinding Lights”\] starts. It feels like it’s coming up before going into the story and into the vision.

**Fresh:** When he did this, it wasn’t just Abel anymore. He created a persona and took this guy through a whole experience. I had never seen someone take on a character like that for an entire year.

**Tesfaye:** People were asking me if I was hurt physically, if I was mentally OK.

**Lipman:** There really is no detail too small in every moment and every performance.

**Fresh:** Abel is one of the biggest stars in the world, so to be the guy that’s responsible for producing that look and having some creative input in the concept, it’s pretty awesome. He did the best job since Michael Jackson did that red jacket.

The pandemic was awful, but seeing happy videos going viral of people dancing in the midst of the madness was really inspiring to see.

**Slaiby:** People wanted a song that was emotional but at the same time made you get up and dance and just feel free. I think “Blinding Lights” has all these feelings.

**Lipman:** It helped us get through a very, very difficult and dark period. The record brought so much joy and essentially brought people together, and it’s something that I’ve said to Abel, “You should be incredibly proud of.”

![The Weeknd](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/feature-the-weeknd-billboard-2021-bb16-brian-ziff-4-650.jpg?w=650)

Rick Owens jacket, Tom Ford shirt, Saint Laurent pants, Bottega Veneta shoes. Photographed by Brian Ziff

**Jon Zellner, president of programming ­operations, iHeartMedia:** If you think about songs that \[cross over and succeed at different radio formats\], you have this evolution that sometimes fizzles out. And that wasn’t the case with this song because it’s so melodic, it’s so memorable, and there’s so much mass appeal.

It probably would be too ambitious for me prior. I knew what I liked, but I felt like I didn’t have the skill sets to deliver that type of project until now.

And they’re stuck in this purgatory state, which I always imagined would be like being stuck in traffic waiting to reach the light at the end of the tunnel. ![The Weeknd](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/feature-the-weeknd-billboard-2021-bb16-brian-ziff-5-650.jpg?w=650)

Photographed by Brian Ziff

"**Can't Feel My Face**" is a song by the Canadian singer-songwriter [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") from his second studio album, _[Beauty Behind the Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_Behind_the_Madness "Beauty Behind the Madness")_ (2015). The song was released on June 8, 2015, as the album's third single. It was written by [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin"), [Peter Svensson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Svensson "Peter Svensson"), [Ali Payami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Payami "Ali Payami"), [Savan Kotecha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savan_Kotecha "Savan Kotecha") and the Weeknd, and produced by Martin and Payami.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

Critics lauded "Can't Feel My Face", comparing the sound of the song to the works of [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson"); _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked it as the best song of 2015. It was also nominated for two [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"): [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_of_the_Year "Record of the Year") and [Best Pop Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Pop_Solo_Performance "Best Pop Solo Performance"). The song experienced commercial success, peaking at number one on both the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), and was certified diamond by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) for selling more than ten million copies in the country.

Elsewhere, "Can't Feel My Face" peaked at number one in Mexico, New Zealand, Denmark, Ireland and South Africa, and was a top 10 single in other territories, such as Australia, the Netherlands, Norway and the United Kingdom.

## Background and composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Can%27t_Feel_My_Face&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and composition")\]

"Can't Feel My Face" leaked in late May 2015.[\[3\]](#cite_note-spin1-3) It was officially released on June 8, 2015, following a performance by the Weeknd at [Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.")'s [Worldwide Developers Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worldwide_Developers_Conference "Worldwide Developers Conference") on the same day.[\[4\]](#cite_note-RS1-4)

The song is composed in the key of [A minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_minor "A minor") and has a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 108 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute"). The [vocal range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_range "Vocal range") spans from E3 to E5.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) Multiple sources have interpreted the song to be about [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine"), including a reference by the Weeknd himself in "[Reminder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reminder_\(song\) "Reminder (song)")": "I just won a new award for a kids show, Talking 'bout a face numbing off a bag of blow".[\[6\]](#cite_note-cocaine-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-telegraph-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) Musically, [Alice Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Vincent "Alice Vincent") of _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ characterised as "a synth-laden, upbeat pop song",[\[7\]](#cite_note-telegraph-7) while Andy Kellman of [AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic") described it as "a sleek slice of retro-modern disco-funk".[\[9\]](#cite_note-AllMusic-9)

The song received widespread critical acclaim. Brennan Carley of _[Spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_\(magazine\) "Spin (magazine)")_ called it "pop perfection", "a thoroughly definitive, all-in jam" and predicted the song would "reach '[Uptown Funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uptown_Funk "Uptown Funk")' levels of airplay and ubiquity".[\[3\]](#cite_note-spin1-3) Mallory Carra of _[Bustle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bustle_\(magazine\) "Bustle (magazine)")_ called it "the official [song of Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_the_Summer "Song of the Summer") 2015" and wrote that the "song has got it all: Fun, funky, catchy, and it sounds like [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson")."[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time (magazine)")_'s Esther Zuckerman deemed the song a "New Favorite Contender for Song of the Summer" and wrote that the chorus was "infectious".[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) In June 2015, Jason Lipshutz of _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ named it one of the "10 Best Songs of 2015 (So Far)".[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

_[Consequence of Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consequence_of_Sound "Consequence of Sound")_ compared the sound of the song to Michael Jackson.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) _[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_\(magazine\) "Complex (magazine)")_ wrote: "The song has a classic pop feel to it, with The Weeknd channeling a bit of Michael Jackson while crooning over the bouncy, and energetic production from [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin")".[\[14\]](#cite_note-Complex-14) _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")_'s reviewer Renato Pagnani placed it in the Best New Track category and made the same comparison: "Perhaps recognizing just how dead-on Tesfaye's Michael Jackson impersonation was on his cover of "[Dirty Diana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty_Diana "Dirty Diana")", the producers anchor the track with a bassline that could have come from an alternate-dimension "[Thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_\(song\) "Thriller (song)")" produced by New Age composer [Vangelis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vangelis "Vangelis") instead of [Quincy Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy_Jones "Quincy Jones")."[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

The song ended up on multiple year-end lists, with _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ naming "Can't Feel My Face" as the best song of 2015: "It was the "oooooh!" that changed everything. That single ecstatic syllable, slipping out just before each chorus, transformed Abel Tesfaye (a.k.a. the Weeknd) from a cult R&B singer to a full-on pop star – just as decisively as a similar yelp of joy marked a new era in Michael Jackson's career when "[Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Stop_'Til_You_Get_Enough "Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough")" hit 36 years earlier. Max Martin's satin-smooth production helped, too, vaulting "Can't Feel My Face" straight to Number One on the pop charts with Scandinavian efficiency. But Tesfaye's showstopping vocal performance is what makes it an instant classic. He spends the song remaking himself as a pop giant – cleverly disguising his obsession with drugs beneath a metaphor about a dangerously hot fling, and playing down his angst-y tendencies until there's just a hint of existential pain in his lighter-than-air falsetto. By the time the song is over, you'll do anything for another hit."[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ also picked "Can't Feel My Face" as the best song of 2015 on its year-end critics' picks: "The Weeknd's irresistible, Michael Jackson-esque "Can't Feel My Face" is so perfectly crafted that it's impossible to imagine a world or alternate reality in which this song isn't No. 1. There are enough hooks in this one single for a dozen chart-toppers, but Abel Tesfaye packed them all into three-and-a-half minutes of sheer ecstasy..."[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ also chose it as the best song of the year: "Everybody with any sort of access to a computer, television, or radio has heard that song seven billion times, and yet it still manages to sound bracing and fresh every time. It's a remarkable accomplishment."[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) _[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")_ ranked it at number 4 on its "The 50 Best Pop Songs Of 2015" list: "I'm still not convinced Abel Tesfaye will be this generation's Michael Jackson, but he does an extremely good impression."[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) _[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_\(website\) "Vulture (website)")_ ranked it at number 8 on its "The 10 Best Songs of 2015" list: "An infectious bassline that trembles like a rubber pencil propels an ex-underground R&B lothario's triumphant transformation from neo-[Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_\(musician\) "Prince (musician)") to neo-MJ."[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) _[MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")_ placed it on its "Best Songs Of 2015" list: "This was The Weeknd proving that he could hit Michael Jackson pop frequencies, while crafting a chart-topper that's uniquely his own."[\[21\]](#cite_note-21) _[Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Village_Voice "Village Voice")_ named "Can't Feel My Face" the third-best single released in 2015 on their annual year-end critics' poll, [Pazz & Jop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pazz_&_Jop "Pazz & Jop").[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ ranked it at number 43 on their "The Best Songs Of The Decade: The 2010s" list: "'Can't Feel My Face' was a bold move for The Weeknd – though not because it took risks musically. This hulking chunk of space-age disco-funk was always destined to top the charts."[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) In 2021, _[Mixmag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixmag "Mixmag")_ placed the song on its "The 30 Best Songs About Cocaine" list.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)

"Can't Feel My Face" debuted at number 24 on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), making a Hot Shot Debut on the chart; it was the Weeknd's third Hot Shot Debut in a year after his previous singles "The Hills" and "[Earned It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earned_It "Earned It")". It produced first-week digital sales of 93,000 units and garnered 4.2 million US streams and 38 million airplay audiences.[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) In its third week on the chart, the song reached number six on the Hot 100, making it his third top 10 hit, and his second solo top 10 hit. After three weeks at number two, "Can't Feel My Face" ascended to number one on the Hot 100, replacing [OMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omi_\(singer\) "Omi (singer)")'s "[Cheerleader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheerleader_\(Omi_song\) "Cheerleader (Omi song)")" and becoming the Weeknd's first number-one single on that chart. It spent three non-consecutive weeks in three separate runs at the top of the _Billboard_ Hot 100, becoming the sixth song to achieve this feat, and the first song to do so since [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars")'s "[Grenade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenade_\(song\) "Grenade (song)")" in 2011. In its third week at number one, "[The Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hills_\(song\) "The Hills (song)")" reached number two, becoming the first act since [The Black Eyed Peas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Black_Eyed_Peas "The Black Eyed Peas") to attain the top two positions on the Hot 100 as a lead artist.[\[26\]](#cite_note-26) The following week, "The Hills" topped the chart, making the Weeknd the first artist since [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") to replace themselves at the top spot; "Can't Feel My Face" fell to number three. It spent nineteen weeks in the chart's top ten before dropping out on November 21, 2015. As of March 2016, it has sold 2,413,488 copies in the US.[\[27\]](#cite_note-us_sales-27)

It debuted in Australia on June 20 at number 27.[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) It later peaked at number two on that chart. In New Zealand, the song debuted at number 12 on June 22 and spent four non-consecutive weeks at number two, before reaching number one in its ninth week on the chart.[\[29\]](#cite_note-NZ_peak-29) In the United Kingdom, "Can't Feel My Face" debuted at number 34, two weeks after "The Hills" had debuted on the chart. It later peaked at number three, becoming the Weeknd's second top 10 single in the country (after "[Earned It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earned_It "Earned It")" peaked at number four earlier in the year), and was also his highest-charting single in the country at the time.\[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_\]

In France, the song debuted at number 59, becoming his highest-entry in solo in the country. Several weeks later, the song reached the top five, becoming his second top five after "[Earned It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earned_It "Earned It")" earlier at that time, and stayed 43 weeks on the [French Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SNEP "SNEP"). The track was later certified gold for 75,000 units sold, becoming his second after "Earned It".[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

The song also reached the top five in others countries, along with United Kingdom and France, peaking at number 1 in South Africa, Ireland, Mexico and Denmark, becoming his first number one for the latter, number 2 in Czech Republic and Slovakia, number 3 in the Netherlands and number 5 in Norway. The song also peaked the top ten in Sweden, Switzerland, Poland, Portugal, Russia and Italy and top twenty in Belgium, Finland, Hungary, South Korea, Spain and Germany.

The accompanying music video, directed by [Grant Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Singer "Grant Singer"), was released on July 29, 2015, on [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music"). As of 2026, the video has received over one billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), becoming the third most-viewed video by the Weeknd behind "The Hills" and "[Starboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(song\) "Starboy (song)")".[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) It begins with the Weeknd singing in a bar to an unimpressed audience, with the exception of his love interest (played by [Chanel Iman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chanel_Iman "Chanel Iman")[\[32\]](#cite_note-idolator1-32)), until a man (played by [Rick Wilder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mau-Mau's "The Mau-Mau's"), who appeared in "The Hills" video), arrives and sets him on fire. The entire crowd, including the love interest, then stand up and starts to dance. The video ends with the Weeknd running out of the bar, still burning.

_[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time (magazine)")_'s reviewer Nolan Feeney wrote that the Weeknd "shines the spotlight on Tesfaye as he delivers a (literally) explosive performance".[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) For Bianca Gracie of _[Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")_, "the usually-moody singer is refreshingly energetic".[\[32\]](#cite_note-idolator1-32) Jon Blistein of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ deemed the video "simple but riveting".[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) [Slava Pastuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slava_Pastuk "Slava Pastuk") of [Noisey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noisey "Noisey") called the video "a bit corny, but weirdly great?"[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")_'s Brian Mansfield wrote: "Like his previous video for The Hills, it's sometimes troubling clip, full of fire and mayhem".[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) Jason Lipshutz of _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ opined that the video is "certainly a sonic homage to MJ, and watching the Weeknd strut around ablaze is an eery \[sic\] coincidence".[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) Similarly, Michelle Geslani of _[Consequence of Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consequence_of_Sound "Consequence of Sound")_ wrote: "Abel Tesfaye is seen busting a couple of moves—no doubt, again, channeling Michael Jackson".[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) Eric Diep of [BET](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BET "BET") also described the video as an "homage to Michael Jackson", noting similarities in the vocals and dance moves.[\[39\]](#cite_note-39)

An alternate music video was released on September 2, 2021.[\[40\]](#cite_note-40)

[The Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") performed "Can't Feel My Face" live for the first time at [Apple WWDC 2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worldwide_Developers_Conference "Worldwide Developers Conference"), the day before its digital release. On July 10, [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") invited the Weeknd on stage for her [1989 World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_World_Tour "1989 World Tour") in [East Rutherford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rutherford "East Rutherford") at the [MetLife Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MetLife_Stadium "MetLife Stadium").[\[41\]](#cite_note-41) The song was performed live on television for the first time at the [2015 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2015 MTV Video Music Awards").[\[42\]](#cite_note-42) The Weeknd also sang it during [Victoria's Secret Fashion Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria's_Secret_Fashion_Show_2015 "Victoria's Secret Fashion Show 2015"), which aired on December 8, 2015.[\[43\]](#cite_note-43)

The Weeknd also performed a part of the song at the [Super Bowl LV halftime show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LV_halftime_show "Super Bowl LV halftime show").

"**Can't Feel My Face**" is a song by the Canadian singer-songwriter [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") from his second studio album, _[Beauty Behind the Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_Behind_the_Madness "Beauty Behind the Madness")_ (2015). The song was released on June 8, 2015, as the album's third single. It was written by [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin"), [Peter Svensson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Svensson "Peter Svensson"), [Ali Payami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Payami "Ali Payami"), [Savan Kotecha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savan_Kotecha "Savan Kotecha") and the Weeknd, and produced by Martin and Payami.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

Critics lauded "Can't Feel My Face", comparing the sound of the song to the works of [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson"); _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked it as the best song of 2015. It was also nominated for two [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"): [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_of_the_Year "Record of the Year") and [Best Pop Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Pop_Solo_Performance "Best Pop Solo Performance"). The song experienced commercial success, peaking at number one on both the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), and was certified diamond by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) for selling more than ten million copies in the country.

Elsewhere, "Can't Feel My Face" peaked at number one in Mexico, New Zealand, Denmark, Ireland and South Africa, and was a top 10 single in other territories, such as Australia, the Netherlands, Norway and the United Kingdom.

## Background and composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Can%27t_Feel_My_Face&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and composition")\]

"Can't Feel My Face" leaked in late May 2015.[\[3\]](#cite_note-spin1-3) It was officially released on June 8, 2015, following a performance by the Weeknd at [Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.")'s [Worldwide Developers Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worldwide_Developers_Conference "Worldwide Developers Conference") on the same day.[\[4\]](#cite_note-RS1-4)

The song is composed in the key of [A minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_minor "A minor") and has a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 108 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute"). The [vocal range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_range "Vocal range") spans from E3 to E5.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) Multiple sources have interpreted the song to be about [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine"), including a reference by the Weeknd himself in "[Reminder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reminder_\(song\) "Reminder (song)")": "I just won a new award for a kids show, Talking 'bout a face numbing off a bag of blow".[\[6\]](#cite_note-cocaine-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-telegraph-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) Musically, [Alice Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Vincent "Alice Vincent") of _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ characterised as "a synth-laden, upbeat pop song",[\[7\]](#cite_note-telegraph-7) while Andy Kellman of [AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic") described it as "a sleek slice of retro-modern disco-funk".[\[9\]](#cite_note-AllMusic-9)

The song received widespread critical acclaim. Brennan Carley of _[Spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_\(magazine\) "Spin (magazine)")_ called it "pop perfection", "a thoroughly definitive, all-in jam" and predicted the song would "reach '[Uptown Funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uptown_Funk "Uptown Funk")' levels of airplay and ubiquity".[\[3\]](#cite_note-spin1-3) Mallory Carra of _[Bustle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bustle_\(magazine\) "Bustle (magazine)")_ called it "the official [song of Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_the_Summer "Song of the Summer") 2015" and wrote that the "song has got it all: Fun, funky, catchy, and it sounds like [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson")."[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time (magazine)")_'s Esther Zuckerman deemed the song a "New Favorite Contender for Song of the Summer" and wrote that the chorus was "infectious".[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) In June 2015, Jason Lipshutz of _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ named it one of the "10 Best Songs of 2015 (So Far)".[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

_[Consequence of Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consequence_of_Sound "Consequence of Sound")_ compared the sound of the song to Michael Jackson.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) _[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_\(magazine\) "Complex (magazine)")_ wrote: "The song has a classic pop feel to it, with The Weeknd channeling a bit of Michael Jackson while crooning over the bouncy, and energetic production from [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin")".[\[14\]](#cite_note-Complex-14) _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")_'s reviewer Renato Pagnani placed it in the Best New Track category and made the same comparison: "Perhaps recognizing just how dead-on Tesfaye's Michael Jackson impersonation was on his cover of "[Dirty Diana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty_Diana "Dirty Diana")", the producers anchor the track with a bassline that could have come from an alternate-dimension "[Thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_\(song\) "Thriller (song)")" produced by New Age composer [Vangelis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vangelis "Vangelis") instead of [Quincy Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy_Jones "Quincy Jones")."[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

The song ended up on multiple year-end lists, with _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ naming "Can't Feel My Face" as the best song of 2015: "It was the "oooooh!" that changed everything. That single ecstatic syllable, slipping out just before each chorus, transformed Abel Tesfaye (a.k.a. the Weeknd) from a cult R&B singer to a full-on pop star – just as decisively as a similar yelp of joy marked a new era in Michael Jackson's career when "[Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Stop_'Til_You_Get_Enough "Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough")" hit 36 years earlier. Max Martin's satin-smooth production helped, too, vaulting "Can't Feel My Face" straight to Number One on the pop charts with Scandinavian efficiency. But Tesfaye's showstopping vocal performance is what makes it an instant classic. He spends the song remaking himself as a pop giant – cleverly disguising his obsession with drugs beneath a metaphor about a dangerously hot fling, and playing down his angst-y tendencies until there's just a hint of existential pain in his lighter-than-air falsetto. By the time the song is over, you'll do anything for another hit."[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ also picked "Can't Feel My Face" as the best song of 2015 on its year-end critics' picks: "The Weeknd's irresistible, Michael Jackson-esque "Can't Feel My Face" is so perfectly crafted that it's impossible to imagine a world or alternate reality in which this song isn't No. 1. There are enough hooks in this one single for a dozen chart-toppers, but Abel Tesfaye packed them all into three-and-a-half minutes of sheer ecstasy..."[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ also chose it as the best song of the year: "Everybody with any sort of access to a computer, television, or radio has heard that song seven billion times, and yet it still manages to sound bracing and fresh every time. It's a remarkable accomplishment."[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) _[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")_ ranked it at number 4 on its "The 50 Best Pop Songs Of 2015" list: "I'm still not convinced Abel Tesfaye will be this generation's Michael Jackson, but he does an extremely good impression."[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) _[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_\(website\) "Vulture (website)")_ ranked it at number 8 on its "The 10 Best Songs of 2015" list: "An infectious bassline that trembles like a rubber pencil propels an ex-underground R&B lothario's triumphant transformation from neo-[Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_\(musician\) "Prince (musician)") to neo-MJ."[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) _[MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV")_ placed it on its "Best Songs Of 2015" list: "This was The Weeknd proving that he could hit Michael Jackson pop frequencies, while crafting a chart-topper that's uniquely his own."[\[21\]](#cite_note-21) _[Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Village_Voice "Village Voice")_ named "Can't Feel My Face" the third-best single released in 2015 on their annual year-end critics' poll, [Pazz & Jop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pazz_&_Jop "Pazz & Jop").[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ ranked it at number 43 on their "The Best Songs Of The Decade: The 2010s" list: "'Can't Feel My Face' was a bold move for The Weeknd – though not because it took risks musically. This hulking chunk of space-age disco-funk was always destined to top the charts."[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) In 2021, _[Mixmag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixmag "Mixmag")_ placed the song on its "The 30 Best Songs About Cocaine" list.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)

"Can't Feel My Face" debuted at number 24 on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), making a Hot Shot Debut on the chart; it was the Weeknd's third Hot Shot Debut in a year after his previous singles "The Hills" and "[Earned It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earned_It "Earned It")". It produced first-week digital sales of 93,000 units and garnered 4.2 million US streams and 38 million airplay audiences.[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) In its third week on the chart, the song reached number six on the Hot 100, making it his third top 10 hit, and his second solo top 10 hit. After three weeks at number two, "Can't Feel My Face" ascended to number one on the Hot 100, replacing [OMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omi_\(singer\) "Omi (singer)")'s "[Cheerleader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheerleader_\(Omi_song\) "Cheerleader (Omi song)")" and becoming the Weeknd's first number-one single on that chart. It spent three non-consecutive weeks in three separate runs at the top of the _Billboard_ Hot 100, becoming the sixth song to achieve this feat, and the first song to do so since [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars")'s "[Grenade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenade_\(song\) "Grenade (song)")" in 2011. In its third week at number one, "[The Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hills_\(song\) "The Hills (song)")" reached number two, becoming the first act since [The Black Eyed Peas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Black_Eyed_Peas "The Black Eyed Peas") to attain the top two positions on the Hot 100 as a lead artist.[\[26\]](#cite_note-26) The following week, "The Hills" topped the chart, making the Weeknd the first artist since [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") to replace themselves at the top spot; "Can't Feel My Face" fell to number three. It spent nineteen weeks in the chart's top ten before dropping out on November 21, 2015. As of March 2016, it has sold 2,413,488 copies in the US.[\[27\]](#cite_note-us_sales-27)

It debuted in Australia on June 20 at number 27.[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) It later peaked at number two on that chart. In New Zealand, the song debuted at number 12 on June 22 and spent four non-consecutive weeks at number two, before reaching number one in its ninth week on the chart.[\[29\]](#cite_note-NZ_peak-29) In the United Kingdom, "Can't Feel My Face" debuted at number 34, two weeks after "The Hills" had debuted on the chart. It later peaked at number three, becoming the Weeknd's second top 10 single in the country (after "[Earned It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earned_It "Earned It")" peaked at number four earlier in the year), and was also his highest-charting single in the country at the time.\[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_\]

In France, the song debuted at number 59, becoming his highest-entry in solo in the country. Several weeks later, the song reached the top five, becoming his second top five after "[Earned It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earned_It "Earned It")" earlier at that time, and stayed 43 weeks on the [French Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SNEP "SNEP"). The track was later certified gold for 75,000 units sold, becoming his second after "Earned It".[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

The song also reached the top five in others countries, along with United Kingdom and France, peaking at number 1 in South Africa, Ireland, Mexico and Denmark, becoming his first number one for the latter, number 2 in Czech Republic and Slovakia, number 3 in the Netherlands and number 5 in Norway. The song also peaked the top ten in Sweden, Switzerland, Poland, Portugal, Russia and Italy and top twenty in Belgium, Finland, Hungary, South Korea, Spain and Germany.

The accompanying music video, directed by [Grant Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Singer "Grant Singer"), was released on July 29, 2015, on [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music"). As of 2026, the video has received over one billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), becoming the third most-viewed video by the Weeknd behind "The Hills" and "[Starboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starboy_\(song\) "Starboy (song)")".[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) It begins with the Weeknd singing in a bar to an unimpressed audience, with the exception of his love interest (played by [Chanel Iman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chanel_Iman "Chanel Iman")[\[32\]](#cite_note-idolator1-32)), until a man (played by [Rick Wilder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mau-Mau's "The Mau-Mau's"), who appeared in "The Hills" video), arrives and sets him on fire. The entire crowd, including the love interest, then stand up and starts to dance. The video ends with the Weeknd running out of the bar, still burning.

_[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time (magazine)")_'s reviewer Nolan Feeney wrote that the Weeknd "shines the spotlight on Tesfaye as he delivers a (literally) explosive performance".[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) For Bianca Gracie of _[Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")_, "the usually-moody singer is refreshingly energetic".[\[32\]](#cite_note-idolator1-32) Jon Blistein of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ deemed the video "simple but riveting".[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) [Slava Pastuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slava_Pastuk "Slava Pastuk") of [Noisey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noisey "Noisey") called the video "a bit corny, but weirdly great?"[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")_'s Brian Mansfield wrote: "Like his previous video for The Hills, it's sometimes troubling clip, full of fire and mayhem".[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) Jason Lipshutz of _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ opined that the video is "certainly a sonic homage to MJ, and watching the Weeknd strut around ablaze is an eery \[sic\] coincidence".[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) Similarly, Michelle Geslani of _[Consequence of Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consequence_of_Sound "Consequence of Sound")_ wrote: "Abel Tesfaye is seen busting a couple of moves—no doubt, again, channeling Michael Jackson".[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) Eric Diep of [BET](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BET "BET") also described the video as an "homage to Michael Jackson", noting similarities in the vocals and dance moves.[\[39\]](#cite_note-39)

An alternate music video was released on September 2, 2021.[\[40\]](#cite_note-40)

[The Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") performed "Can't Feel My Face" live for the first time at [Apple WWDC 2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worldwide_Developers_Conference "Worldwide Developers Conference"), the day before its digital release. On July 10, [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") invited the Weeknd on stage for her [1989 World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_World_Tour "1989 World Tour") in [East Rutherford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Rutherford "East Rutherford") at the [MetLife Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MetLife_Stadium "MetLife Stadium").[\[41\]](#cite_note-41) The song was performed live on television for the first time at the [2015 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2015 MTV Video Music Awards").[\[42\]](#cite_note-42) The Weeknd also sang it during [Victoria's Secret Fashion Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria's_Secret_Fashion_Show_2015 "Victoria's Secret Fashion Show 2015"), which aired on December 8, 2015.[\[43\]](#cite_note-43)

The Weeknd also performed a part of the song at the [Super Bowl LV halftime show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LV_halftime_show "Super Bowl LV halftime show").

## Martin Garrix remix

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Can%27t_Feel_My_Face&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Martin Garrix remix")\]

On November 6, 2015, [Martin Garrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Garrix "Martin Garrix") released a remix of the song through [XO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XO_\(record_label\) "XO (record label)") lasting 4 minutes and 12 seconds.[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) The remix was featured on the Japanese edition of _[Beauty Behind the Madness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty_Behind_the_Madness "Beauty Behind the Madness")_.[\[45\]](#cite_note-45)

*   On July 27, 2015, actor [Tom Cruise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Cruise "Tom Cruise") performed to "Can't Feel My Face" in a "Lip Sync Battle" on _[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")_.[\[46\]](#cite_note-46)[\[47\]](#cite_note-47)
*   The song is also featured in the 2015 video game _[Madden NFL 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madden_NFL_16 "Madden NFL 16")_.[\[48\]](#cite_note-48)
*   Singer [Stevie Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder") performed a parody of the song during a surprise pop-up concert at Central Park's SummerStage in New York City, August 17, 2015.[\[49\]](#cite_note-49)
*   NASCAR driver [David Ragan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ragan "David Ragan") posted a video lip syncing the song to his No. 55 Toyota in response to a commonly asked question "What is it like driving a NASCAR Sprint Cup car?"[\[50\]](#cite_note-50)[\[51\]](#cite_note-51)

*   The song was featured in the 2015 [YouTube Rewind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_Rewind "YouTube Rewind") as part of the video's soundtrack.
*   On September 15, 2015, during a game of "The Wheel Of Musical Impersonations" on _The Tonight Show starring Jimmy Fallon_, [Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Fallon "Jimmy Fallon") sang "Can't Feel My Face" in the style of [Sting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sting_\(musician\) "Sting (musician)"), and [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande") sang it in the style of [Céline Dion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Céline_Dion "Céline Dion").
*   The song also appeared in a [season 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_\(season_2\) "Empire (season 2)") episode of hit [soap opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soap_opera "Soap opera") _[Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_\(2015_TV_series\) "Empire (2015 TV series)")_ called "Be True", aired on October 21, 2015.
*   Jay McGuiness and Aliona Vilani danced their showdance to "Can't Feel My Face" in the 2015 _[Strictly Come Dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strictly_Come_Dancing "Strictly Come Dancing")_ finale on December 19, 2015.
*   The song is also featured in other television shows including _[Being Mary Jane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Being_Mary_Jane "Being Mary Jane")_, _[Cooper Barrett's Guide to Surviving Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooper_Barrett's_Guide_to_Surviving_Life "Cooper Barrett's Guide to Surviving Life")_, _[Younger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Younger_\(TV_series\) "Younger (TV series)")_, _[Superstore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superstore_\(TV_series\) "Superstore (TV series)"),_ and _[The Real O'Neals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Real_O'Neals "The Real O'Neals")_.
*   The song is also featured in the rhythm game _[Just Dance 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_Dance_2017 "Just Dance 2017")_.
*   On the October 22, 2019, episode of reality television singing competition show _[The Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Voice_\(American_season_17\) "The Voice (American season 17)")_, Team [Gwen (Stefani)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwen_Stefani "Gwen Stefani") members Jessie Lawrence and Rose Short performed an arrangement of the song in a Battle round.
*   A cover of the song by [Kiana Ledé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiana_Ledé "Kiana Ledé") is played in the 2021 animated film _[Sing 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sing_2 "Sing 2")_.

# Why the Lyrics to Ariana Grande’s New Single—And So Many Pop Hits—Make No Sense

[Brow Beat](/culture/brow-beat)

## The Most Puzzling, Ungrammatical Lyrics of Hitmaker Max Martin

July 09, 20148:32 AM

![ariana grande](https://compote.slate.com/images/c683dbe9-6e4e-4d07-9473-f5757d989845.jpg?crop=590%2C380%2Cx0%2Cy0)

It’s not Ariana Grande’s fault her lyrics don’t make sense.

Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images

The grammar police were out in full force on Monday after Ariana Grande released the _Star Wars_–inspired [lyric video](http://www.idolator.com/7525667/ariana-grande-break-free-lyric-video?utm_source=sc-tw&utm_medium=ref&utm_campaign=agrande) to her ­new single, “Break Free.”

Grande’s voice trails off a bit, so it’s hard to tell whether she’s fudging the conjugation of “to be” for the approximate rhyme, or perhaps trying to say “am” in such a way that it almost, somehow, rhymes with “heart.” But even if we let her off the hook for that one, the song gives us more baffling lines to chew on. “I only want to die alive,” she belts, “never by the hands of a broken heart.” Where to begin? That it’s impossible to die alive? That hearts don’t have hands?

The grammatical bar for pop lyrics is plenty low, but some effort, at least, is required to clear it. And while we are fairly forgiving when it comes to the grammar of pop songs, we expect them at least to be fairly idiomatic most of the time. The lines above don’t sound like someone who’s careless about grammar. They sound like someone who is not a native English speaker and is _also_ careless about grammar.

As it happens, the man behind many of the mega-hits of the last two decades, and also this song, is writer-producer Max Martin, who is from Sweden. Martin co-wrote and produced dozens of hit singles for Britney Spears, ‘N Sync, the Backstreet Boys, Pink, and Katy Perry, among other _Billboard_ chart-toppers. And a number of his co-writers—Andreas Carlsson, Jorgen Elofsson, Per Magnusson, David Kreuger, Denniz Pop—also hail from the land of ABBA and lingonberries.

Martin and his compatriots aren’t the only songwriters churning out lyrics with occasionally head-scratching foreign syntax. Owen Pallett wrote a few months ago in **_Slate_** about the “[specifically Francophonic idiosyncrasy](https://www.slate.com/articles/arts/culturebox/2014/03/daft_punk_s_get_lucky_explained_using_music_theory.html)” in Daft Punk’s use of the word “good” in “[Get Lucky](http://www.amazon.com/dp/B00CRMX53S/?tag=slatmaga-20).” But a look back through the Martin catalogs yields a veritable treasure trove of lyrics that your third-grade English teacher would shake her head at.

Now, since Martin often works with co-writers, it can be difficult to tell which specific lyrics he is personally responsible for. But he is the common denominator in all this lyrical clumsiness. And so, below, we’ve rounded up some of our favorite ungrammatical, unidiomatic, or just plain awkward lines from songs by the Swedish hitmaker.

**“I live my life the way/ To keep you comin’ back to me”**

_“Quit Playing Games (With My Heart),” Backstreet Boys, 1995. Written by Max Martin and Herbert Crichlow._**“We’ve got it goin’ on for years”**

 _“We’ve Got It Goin’ On,” 1996, Backstreet Boys. Written by Denniz Pop, Max Martin, and Herbert Crichlow._

**“Tell me, I’m not in the blue”**

_“(You Drive Me) Crazy,” Britney Spears, 1999. Written by Jorgen Elofsson, Per Magnusson, David Kreuger, and Max Martin._**“Sadness is beautiful/ loneliness is tragical”**  

_“Shape of My Heart,” Backstreet Boys, 2000. Written by Max Martin, Rami Yacoub, and Lisa Miskovsky._  
**“Add on my uncanny ego/ No one’s less humbled than I”**

_“Bigger,” Backstreet Boys, 2009. Written by Max Martin, Shellback, and Tiffany Amber._**“I kept taking/ Taking the blame/ And it’s soring me up inside”**

_“Outta My Head,” Leona Lewis, 2009. Written by Max Martin and Shellback._

 **“See I know a little bit something good/ Always comes out of a little bit something bad”**

 _“First Love,” Jennifer Lopez, 2014. Written by Max Martin, Savan Kotecha, and Ilya Salmanzadeh._**“I only wanna die alive/ Never by the hands of a broken heart/ Don’t wanna hear you lie tonight/ Now that I’ve become who I really are”**

_“Break Free,” Ariana Grande featuring Zedd, 2014. Written by Anton Zaslavski, Max Martin, and Savan Kotecha._
